You have canceled on the MAGA movement?| | | **You canceled on the MAGA movement?** I just got out of a midterm strategy briefing, and that’s what I was told. _You’ve been with me since 2016._ You’re one of the real ones who have stood with me through the witch hunts, impeachments, investigations, everything. We have accomplished so much together, and we are almost to the finish line of Making America Great Again! **_But that cannot happen without you._** So when my team told me you still haven’t re-pledged this year... I had to check. Is that true?

They’re already planning the next impeachment. And let’s be clear: the fight is nowhere near over. **Our majority is thinner than a sheet of paper.** Critical seats are on the line. If they flip even a handful, they’ll have the numbers to come after me again impeachment, investigations, the whole playbook. body:
Democrats Are Underfunding the Races That Could Remake the Map

Democrats: With just weeks to go until Election Day, Politico just published an article highlighting a major problem Democrats may have in taking advantage of what could be a historic cycle.
All across the country, donations small and large are pouring into the marquee U.S. Senate and House races, but Democratic candidates in state races that could remake the map are going underfunded.
Nevada is one of those states. This is a state where we can flip a governor's race and the State House. Think of re-taking control of the branches of government there as a form of Trump Insurance should he try to steal the 2028 election.
**[Please split a contribution between six Nevada state legislative candidates in important races.](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/12310?source=em261003&t=1&akid=3060%2E4767699%2EWMpzr0)**
\- Gavin Newsom
[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/12310?source=em261003&t=2&akid=3060%2E4767699%2EWMpzr0)
* * *

[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/12310?source=em261003&t=3&akid=3060%2E4767699%2EWMpzr0)
**Democrats Are Underfunding the Races That Could Remake the Map**
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/12310?source=em261003&t=4&akid=3060%2E4767699%2EWMpzr0)
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. — Major Democratic contributors and small-dollar givers are flooding Senate hopefuls with cash, but in some of the most politically crucial states they could lose winnable gubernatorial races because they’re being so dramatically outspent by Republican nominees and their allied groups.
In former and future presidential battlegrounds Florida, Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Wisconsin and Nevada, the gubernatorial advertising gap is yawning. For the remainder of the campaign, Republicans are on track to outspend Democrats on television about 6-to-1 in Florida, more than 3-to-1 in Texas, 2.5-to-1 in Georgia, more than 2-to-1 in Wisconsin, and only slightly more narrowly in Ohio and Nevada. ...
Liberal donors swooning over Senate races is not a new phenomenon. But it has accelerated in the age of Trump, and with decidedly mixed results.
Checking the president by controlling Congress is easy to grasp, short enough to fit on a bumper sticker with the right brevity. Nothing animates Democrats like confronting Trump, and flipping the House and Senate does as much.
Also, the attendant Washington-heavy focus of the media, along with social media algorithms that push what draws clicks, means most political hobbyists can tell you the name of big-state Senate candidates but not the party’s gubernatorial nominees (looking at you, Texas).
The problem is compounded for Democrats in capitals where they’re out of power, and have been for decades, because the transactional money from interests with business before state government will be overwhelmingly directed to the incumbent party. ...
But the left should know better by now. The aftermath of 2020 and the unsubtle steps the president is taking now to seize election machinery should have underscored the importance of state and local elections, particularly for those officers counting or certifying election results.
More consequential, however, are the long-term implications of gubernatorial races this year.
If Democrats can win contests in red-tinted states next month, particularly across the Sun Belt, they’ll have a stronger infrastructure to be competitive in the 2028 presidential race. They would, in other words, have more paths to 270 electoral votes without living and dying with the fate of the blue-wall states across the Great Lakes.

* * *
🇺🇸 🇺🇸 **To my fellow Democrats — Please do not click away.** 🙏 🙏
Democrats have a generational opportunity to flip seats up and down the ballot in states across the country.
But taking advantage of this moment requires people who want to see that happen step up when our Democratic candidates need it most.
Money in these state legislative contests goes a long way. Much further than U.S. Senate and House races.
If everyone reading this split a $ASK contribution between six critical state legislative races we've identified in Nevada, Democrats would take total control in a critical state.
[**If $3 seems worth it to you for Democrats to flip seats everywhere this November, please do what you can to split a donation between six critical state legislative races in Nevada. Please do it today. **](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/12311?source=em261003&t=5&akid=3060%2E4767699%2EWMpzr0)

Also, the attendant Washington-heavy focus of the media, along with social media algorithms that push what draws clicks, means most political hobbyists can tell you the name of big-state Senate candidates but not the party’s gubernatorial nominees (looking at you, Texas). The problem is compounded for Democrats in capitals where they’re out of power, and have been for decades, because the transactional money from interests with business before state government will be overwhelmingly directed to the incumbent party. ... But the left should know better by now. The aftermath of 2020 and the unsubtle steps the president is taking now to seize election machinery should have underscored the importance of state and local elections, particularly for those officers counting or certifying election results. More consequential, however, are the long-term implications of gubernatorial races this year. If Democrats can win contests in red-tinted states next month, particularly across the Sun Belt, they’ll have a stronger infrastructure to be competitive in the 2028 presidential race. They would, in other words, have more paths to 270 electoral votes without living and dying with the fate of the blue-wall states across the Great Lakes. 🇺🇸 🇺🇸 To my fellow Democrats — Please do not click away. 🙏 🙏 Democrats have a generational opportunity to flip seats up and down the ballot in states across the country. But taking advantage of this moment requires people who want to see that happen step up when our Democratic candidates need it most. Money in these state legislative contests goes a long way. Much further than U.S. Senate and House races. If everyone reading this split a $ASK contribution between six critical state legislative races we've identified in Nevada, Democrats would take total control in a critical state. | | |

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Recharging after another long day on the campaign trail
body:
It’s been tough to find escape in my favorite novels lately.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&source=&t=1&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ) | | | |
---
Hi, Peter – hope I’m not interrupting your evening.
The little leisure time I get nowadays is usually spent reading before bed. It’s the one time I get to tune out the stress of real life in the pages of a sci-fi novel or legal thriller. Tonight, it’s John Grisham.
Yet with the way things are going after just two years of unchecked Republican power in Washington DC, some days, these fictional stories seem more believable than our present reality.
That’s a problem – and it’s one of many reasons why I couldn’t sit out of the U.S. Senate race here in North Carolina. Too much is at stake.
Hundreds of thousands of folks have joined us in the fight to flip NC blue for the first time since 2008, and I’m grateful: **Because with exactly 31 days until Election Day, I need all the help I can get to ensure we have the grassroots resources to stand up to the GOP’s increasingly desperate attacks and win.**
[**_So if you haven’t had a chance yet, I’d be honored if you would join us by making a donation toward our daily fundraising goal tonight._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=5&t=8&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=5&t=9&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=25&t=10&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
---
| | [DONATE $50](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=50&t=11&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&t=12&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
---
My nightly routine helps me recharge ahead of long days on the campaign trail. With just weeks left until our election decides Senate control and the future of our country, that’s more important than ever. _So is your support, Peter._
North Carolinians start in-person voting in 12 days, which means time’s running out to reach them with our message and bring them to our side. [**_We won’t have the resources to do that if we come up short on today’s goal, so I’m personally asking: If you can, will you chip in $5 or more to help us cross the finish line before you hit the hay?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=5&t=13&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
| | [DONATE NOW](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&amount=5&t=14&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
---
Thanks for everything – have a good night,
Roy Cooper
_If you've donated via check, mail or in-person event, thank you! Our system may not have processed your gift yet, but rest assured, we have received it. Please note, if you have given through a spouse or another email or phone number, our records may not have transferred that information here. We are grateful for your support and no further action is required at this time._
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&t=2&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1589&source=&t=3&akid=4153%2E124072%2EHwINXQ)

| | | | | My name is Nilus Mattive.

I represent a firm called Weiss Ratings. And for the last 100 years, we've actively warned Americans about every major financial crisis — BEFORE it happened.

Our founder's father, Irving Weiss, used a series of mathematical formulas to predict the Great Depression.

While the rest of the stock market was drunk on profits, Irving tried to warn everyone he knew that a crash was inevitable — and coming soon.

His bosses on Wall Street scoffed at him. They thought he was trying to ruin their business.

But Irving had the last laugh ...

On Oct. 29, 1929, the market dropped 12% — before eventually falling 90% in the next three years.

Irving Weiss — and his small group of followers — not only avoided the crash but were able to profit during the Depression — even while most Americans were in the poorhouse.

Irving's son, Martin Weiss, took those well-established formulas and put loads of computer power behind them, creating algorithms to rate stocks, banks and insurance companies.

Today, our team of analysts, mathematicians and data scientists use his original formulas ...

Combined with new formulas and advanced computer models to cut through the financial fog and detect early warning signals.

These so-called Weiss Ratings predicted the bank failures of the Savings and Loan crisis of the 1980s ahead of time, helping followers avoid chaos.

At the height of the Dot-Com Bubble in 1999 ...

Analysts at big firms like Morgan Stanley ... Bloomberg ... or JPMorgan ...

Kept issuing optimistic reports with hugely inflated valuations ...

And Zacks — a famed stock ratings company — couldn't find a single stock on the Nasdaq to rank a "Sell."

But Weiss Ratings signaled something completely different.

It said 90% of all those stocks were putting investors in great danger ...

Sure enough, the Dot-Com Bubble soon followed, wiping out 77% of stock market wealth and ruining the retirements of millions of Americans who failed to heed our warnings.

In 2008, as overleveraged banks loaded up on below-grade mortgage bonds, Weiss Ratings warned of the crisis to come.

In fact, we accurately predicted 98% of the banks who would eventually fail in the Financial Crisis — missing just one.

Consider the big Bear Stearns failure, for example ...

On Dec. 3, 2007, we published an alert warning that _Bear Stearns ... "[had] sunk its balance sheet even deeper into the hole, with $20.2 billion in dead assets, or 155 percent of its equity, and is threatened with insolvency."_

Bear Stearns collapsed 33 days later.

We also published an article warning that _"Lehman Brothers [was] in similar shape because of an even larger $34.7 billion pile-up of dead assets, or 160 percent of its equity."_

Lehman collapsed 182 days later.

And that single collapse is what ignited the greatest financial crisis since the Great Depression.

We also warned well ahead of time about Washington Mutual, Bank of America, Citigroup and all the major banks that failed or required a bailout.

Weiss Ratings pounded the table for investors, telling them _"DO NOT TOUCH THESE COMPANIES WITH A TEN-FOOT POLE" ..._

While all along, officials on Wall Street and in Washington swore on a stack of bibles that no such failures could EVER be possible.

We know how that played out.

Those who listened to us could have minimized or avoided catastrophic losses ... and the personal pain that comes with it, while ...

Those who owned the shares in those same big banks saw them plunge 96%, 98%, even 100% from their peak value.

Our Weiss Ratings also signaled danger in 2020, during the early days of the Covid outbreak.

Sure enough, stocks plunged 30% in a handful of days after our warning.

That's why a study in the _Wall Street Journal_ reported that Weiss Ratings was the #1 stock rating system for profit performance.

When the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and others commissioned a study to determine which financial ratings company had the best profit track record for stocks ...

Weiss Ratings was number one overall.

That's why hundreds of thousands of investors access our free ratings every day.

While we have a history of spotting danger well ahead of time, I have to say: All those previous crises pale in comparison to what could be coming, thanks to overblown AI hype.

I believe it's like the Great Depression, the Dot-Com Bubble and the 2008 Financial Crisis — _combined._

And it could change our country for the worse — for years to come.

Case File No DRT-ED-AI · Special File · The AI Fingerprint
1929\. 2000. 2008. We Found the Same Fingerprint on the AI Boom.
Record spending, $1.2 trillion in AI-linked debt plus hundreds of billions more off the books, a market resting on a few names, and Washington insisting it’s a golden age. History has seen this setup before. It rarely ends quietly.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Every financial crisis of the last hundred years left the same fingerprint before it hit. Prices ran far ahead of profits. Borrowing hid in places regulators weren’t looking. Fewer and fewer stocks carried the market. And the people closest to the boom kept insisting this time was different. We went looking for that fingerprint in the AI trade. Here’s what’s on the evidence board.
The pattern
| | Three Crashes, One Shape
---|---
| | 1929
---
The margin boom
Stocks bought with borrowed money, a market that only went up, and officials who called the economy sound. The Dow eventually lost close to 90% from its peak.
| | 2000
---
The dot-com bubble
Investment in tech hit record highs while profits lagged far behind. The Nasdaq fell about 78% from March 2000 to October 2002.
| | 2008
---
The leverage crisis
Debt was buried in off-balance-sheet vehicles most investors never saw. When it surfaced, bank stocks lost most, and in some cases all, of their value.
The evidence board
| | What the AI Boom Looks Like Right Now
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the spending.** Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta are on track to spend roughly $700 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, mostly data centers and chips. In early 2026, Goldman Sachs pointed to peak investment spending as the first warning sign from the dot-com era.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
**Exhibit B — the hidden debt.** A draft Treasury analysis obtained by NOTUS in July put visible AI-related corporate debt at about $1.2 trillion, roughly 14% of JPMorgan’s investment-grade index. It cited Moody’s estimate of $662 billion in data-center leases held off balance sheet through special-purpose vehicles funded by private credit. Treasury called the draft “unvetted.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the cash squeeze.** The same analysis projects hyperscalers will plow about 94% of their operating cash flow back into infrastructure by 2026–2027. This week Micron posted a record quarter and its stock still slipped after it announced higher spending: roughly $25 billion in capex in half a year.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the thinning market.** Fewer than half of S&P; 500 stocks trade above their 200-day moving average, down from about 75% in mid-August. The index looks healthy only because a handful of leaders are holding it up.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit E — the cost of money.** In 1999 the Fed cut rates and fueled the rally. In 2026 the Fed has hiked, and the 10-year Treasury hit its highest level since 2002 this week. Every dollar of AI debt now costs more to carry.
Decoder
| | The Line Every Bubble Uses
---|---
| | “Artificial intelligence will be a key driver of America’s new Golden Age.”— Treasury spokesperson, responding to the draft report on AI debt
---|---
What it says
There’s nothing to worry about.
What it means
**Our theory:** AI may well transform the economy, and that’s exactly the problem. The internet did transform the economy, and the Nasdaq still lost 78%. A technology can be real and still be badly overpriced. When officials answer a warning about debt with a promise about the future, they’re not answering the question.
Place your bets
| | Which Crack Shows First?
---|---
A major AI borrower struggles to refinance as yields stay above 5% **35%**
| |
---|---
A hyperscaler cuts its capex plan, and suppliers sell off together **30%**
| |
---|---
Private-credit losses tied to data-center leases surface publicly **20%**
| |
---|---
None of these by year-end: the boom keeps running **15%**
| |
---|---
Our best guesses. The four add up to 100%.
| ClassificationPressure, building
---
The fingerprint is there: record spending, debt hidden off balance sheet, a narrowing market, rising rates and official reassurance. None of that tells you the day the turn comes. It tells you the kind of protection people wished they’d had in 2000 and 2008 is worth looking at before the turn, not after.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileIn 2000 and in 2008, the warning signs were public for months. Why did so few investors act on them in time?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**Because the crowd was still making money.** Warnings sound foolish while prices are rising, and the people who issue them get laughed at, right up until they don’t. **Our theory:** the investors who came through 2000 and 2008 intact didn’t predict the exact day. They decided in advance what they would do when the signals lined up. The signals are lining up now.

body:
Derek, want to know the secret to winning elections?
---
Derek, this is an email from the National Democratic Committee about our work to flip Congress in 30 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9614%2E22930333%2ErqnirD). If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=2&akid=9614%2E22930333%2ErqnirD) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=9614%2E22930333%2ErqnirD), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=4&akid=9614%2E22930333%2ErqnirD). Derek, want to know the secret to winning elections? **_Organize, organize, organize, organize.**_ And that’s exactly what the DNC has been doing:
* Hiring hundreds of organizers to register thousands of new voters in key swing districts.
* Training voter protection teams and recruiting poll watchers to ensure that we immediately take action if any ICE deployments happen near polling sites.
* Deploying thousands of volunteers and organizers to knock doors, make calls, send texts, and get every last Democrat out to vote.

All of these programs _together_ are how Democrats will win — and they’re all funded by supporters like **you.** Over 99% of the DNC’s contributions come from grassroots donors chipping in what they can, when they can. name: Major General Paul Eaton, U.S. Army, retired
subject: New York Times
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
#
Peter: This is Paul Eaton, Retired Army Major General and Senior Advisor of VoteVets.
The New York Times just released an article about our work at VoteVets ahead of the midterm elections. It talks about the urgency of the moment, and the need to elect Veterans who can stand up against the Trump administration.
I’ve attached the article below. Thank you for reading and supporting our work.
| [DONATE](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=1&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
---
* * *
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=2&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
**Antiwar Veterans Group Spends Millions to Elect Democrats, Shaping Midterms**
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=3&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
The Democratic primary for Iowa’s open Senate seat presented exactly the kind of scenario that Jon Soltz, the co-founder of VoteVets, is always searching for: one where his organization could play an outsize role in shaping a race.
Two little-known Democrats were vying for the nomination, in a contest where no outside group was spending. So Mr. Soltz poured money into the campaign of Josh Turek, a state legislator and a former Paralympic gold medalist, who did not serve but was born with spina bifida after his father was exposed to Agent Orange in Vietnam.
The first infusion of cash from VoteVets — $825,000 in March — was more than Mr. Turek’s opponent, Zach Wahls, had on hand at the end of 2025. (VoteVets entered the race only after Nathan Sage, a veteran of the Iraq war, dropped out of the primary.)
And VoteVets kept spending, totaling an eye-popping $9.7 million on digital and television advertising, as well as direct mail, in a race that Mr. Turek won and is now viewed as within reach for Democrats.
The group is shoveling an additional $4.5 million into ads hitting his Republican rival, Representative Ashley Hinson, for her support of the war with Iran. (Ms. Hinson this week called for an “immediate end” to the war after voting a half-dozen times against directing President Trump to halt it.)
It is the starkest example of the extensive role the organization, formed in 2006 to support Democratic veterans running in opposition to the war in Iraq, is playing in shaping this year’s midterm elections as a different conflict in the Middle East has again soured voters on the party in power.
“Iowa is in play because we helped put it in play,” Mr. Soltz said in a wide-ranging interview this month. “If Democrats take back the Senate, it could be because of Iowa, and if that happens, then I can sit here and say this is the most successful cycle VoteVets has ever had.”
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=4&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
Overall, VoteVets plans this year to spend $60 million on 331 Democratic candidates nationwide — 20 House and Senate candidates and 311 down-ballot races — the most since it was founded. That makes it one of the most substantial single-issue advocacy groups operating in the midterm cycle, and one of the main groups spending the most to support Democratic candidates.
The only other such organization that comes close is the United Democracy Project, the super PAC associated with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee that has spent about $54 million so far this cycle and is likely to spend much more.
VoteVets operates independently, but its interests often align with those of the Democratic congressional leaders. It also coordinates with other outside groups on endorsements and then bundles money under its own umbrella. While the majority of the group’s money comes from individual donors, a substantial portion comes from big labor unions and corporate PACs, including those associated with Honeywell, General Motors, General Dynamics and Elevance Health.
“I call candidates all the time, and they can send me donors,” Mr. Soltz said. “Perhaps another organization cares about a race, but we’re the better brand.”
Over the years, the group has expanded its mission beyond supporting veterans to elevating candidates with national security backgrounds as well as people like Mr. Turek, whose lives have been shaped by a family member’s service and who understand a different facet of the human cost of war.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=5&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
VoteVets has spent $1 million on behalf of Cait Conley, who served in combat in Iraq and Afghanistan, a major infusion of cash for a House race.
Mr. Soltz, who served in multiple tours in the Iraq war and other deployments overseas, is currently out to elect a new slate of Democratic veterans, including many women, at a time when opposition to the war in Iran is dragging down Mr. Trump’s approval ratings and bringing Republicans with him.
It is happening as democratic socialist candidates have received outsize attention for defeating establishment contenders in primaries across the country.
But VoteVets’ millions could be a more decisive factor in some of the critical races in which Democrats are looking to unseat Republicans to win control of the House.
In upstate New York, the group has spent $1 million on behalf of Cait Conley, who served in combat in Iraq and Afghanistan, in her race to unseat Representative Mike Lawler, a major infusion of cash for a House race. In Arizona, the group has money on hold to put behind Jo Mendoza, a former Marine drill sergeant running against Representative Juan Ciscomani. In New Jersey, the group is spending $1.2 million for Rebecca Bennett, a Navy veteran looking to unseat Representative Thomas H. Kean Jr. And in Virginia, the group is planning to spend to back Elaine Luria, a Navy veteran, against Representative Jen Kiggans.
VoteVets also played a significant role in financially boosting Luke Bronin, the former Navy intelligence officer who defeated Representative John B. Larson, the 78-year-old Democrat who was seeking a 15th term in his solidly blue district.
“We have no issue with Larson,” Mr. Soltz said. “It’s about the fact that we can get a veteran into Congress for the next 30 years, to be the chairman of the House Veterans Committee or Foreign Affairs. That’s our interest. If you only work in flippable seats, then when the wave comes in, you will lose.”
Special interest groups have long played a prominent role in elections, but some ethics experts said that an organization as powerful as VoteVets could potentially eclipse the candidates themselves.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-oct26.xXsDMU&refcode=em261004-1-180&t=6&akid=35653%2E3013755%2ErI2GhW)
The group is spending $1.2 million for Rebecca Bennett, a Navy veteran looking to unseat Representative Thomas H. Kean Jr. in New Jersey.
“It’s a broader trend where outside groups are coming to just dominate the most competitive races and increasingly competitive primaries,” said Daniel Weiner, the senior director of the Brennan Center’s Elections and Government Program. “That is risky when they start to drown out candidates.”
Still, Mr. Weiner said that VoteVets was the exception in an arena increasingly dominated by outside groups that seek to hide how they are influencing elections, because it runs ads on the issue it actually stands for and has a clear agenda that voters understand.
“That is increasingly not the norm,” Mr. Weiner said. “The norm is more shadowy groups where voters don’t know what it stands for or who is behind them.”
Andrew Mayersohn, a researcher for the watchdog group OpenSecrets, said that he classifies VoteVets as “partially disclosing” its donors, meaning that more than 5 percent of its money comes from sources that are not disclosed. That is because it has its own nonprofit set up under the 501(c)(4) section of the tax code whose donors are not required to be publicly disclosed.
The group has had some setbacks this cycle. It heavily backed Maura Sullivan, a Marine veteran, in a New Hampshire primary she lost to Stefany Shaheen, the daughter of Senator Jeanne Shaheen, a political powerhouse in her state. And in one of Michigan’s most competitive districts, VoteVets backed Matt Maasdam, a former member of the Navy SEALs, in a heated primary he lost to William Lawrence, a progressive activist and co-founder of the Sunrise Movement.
When VoteVets was founded 20 years ago, it was still uncommon for Democrats to attack Republicans on military issues, which had long been seen as one of the G.O.P.’s strongest suits.
The organization burst onto the political scene with a searing ad that showed a mannequin dressed in the body armor given to soldiers in Iraq getting shredded by bullets, and targeted Republicans who voted against a Democratic proposal to provide $1 billion to outfit U.S. troops with more modern equipment.
Representative Pat Ryan, a New York Democrat who completed two tours in Iraq, credits VoteVets with providing the financial and political support for him to win a 2022 special election that many in his party thought was out of reach.
“This linking of military service and fighting for core American freedoms as a thing that the Democratic Party should absolutely, unabashedly own and dominate on is a huge value-add to the party,” Mr. Ryan said in an interview.
“In 2003, I desperately wish there had been leaders who could say, ‘I fought for the country; this is going to make us less safe, less prosperous’ — and to do it right out of the gate,” he said. “I’m super proud that we as vets, with VoteVets driving that, stood from Day Zero of this war in Iran and said, ‘This is bad.’”

Two little-known Democrats were vying for the nomination, in a contest where no outside group was spending. So Mr. Soltz poured money into the campaign of Josh Turek, a state legislator and a former Paralympic gold medalist, who did not serve but was born with spina bifida after his father was exposed to Agent Orange in Vietnam. The first infusion of cash from VoteVets — $825,000 in March — was more than Mr. Turek’s opponent, Zach Wahls, had on hand at the end of 2025. (VoteVets entered the race only after Nathan Sage, a veteran of the Iraq war, dropped out of the primary.) And VoteVets kept spending, totaling an eye-popping $9.7 million on digital and television advertising, as well as direct mail, in a race that Mr. Turek won and is now viewed as within reach for Democrats. The group is shoveling an additional $4.5 million into ads hitting his Republican rival, Representative Ashley Hinson, for her support of the war with Iran. (Ms. Hinson this week called for an “immediate end” to the war after voting a half-dozen times against directing President Trump to halt it.) It is the starkest example of the extensive role the organization, formed in 2006 to support Democratic veterans running in opposition to the war in Iraq, is playing in shaping this year’s midterm elections as a different conflict in the Middle East has again soured voters on the party in power. “Iowa is in play because we helped put it in play,” Mr. Soltz said in a wide-ranging interview this month. “If Democrats take back the Senate, it could be because of Iowa, and if that happens, then I can sit here and say this is the most successful cycle VoteVets has ever had.” Overall, VoteVets plans this year to spend $60 million on 331 Democratic candidates nationwide — 20 House and Senate candidates and 311 down-ballot races — the most since it was founded. That makes it one of the most substantial single-issue advocacy groups operating in the midterm cycle, and one of the main groups spending the most to support Democratic candidates. The only other such organization that comes close is the United Democracy Project, the super PAC associated with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee that has spent about $54 million so far this cycle and is likely to spend much more. VoteVets operates independently, but its interests often align with those of the Democratic congressional leaders. It also coordinates with other outside groups on endorsements and then bundles money under its own umbrella. While the majority of the group’s money comes from individual donors, a substantial portion comes from big labor unions and corporate PACs, including those associated with Honeywell, General Motors, General Dynamics and Elevance Health. “I call candidates all the time, and they can send me donors,” Mr. Soltz said. “Perhaps another organization cares about a race, but we’re the better brand.” Over the years, the group has expanded its mission beyond supporting veterans to elevating candidates with national security backgrounds as well as people like Mr. Turek, whose lives have been shaped by a family member’s service and who understand a different facet of the human cost of war. Today, I’m asking you to make a donation to Roy Cooper’s campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. Across this country, people are hurting in ways that don’t always make the history books but shape lives all the same.
The grocery bills that are too high. A lifesaving prescription that forces a difficult choice. A paycheck that just doesn’t stretch as far as it once did. | These are the real pressures that define a moment.
**Roy Cooper has spent much of his life as a public servant working to ease those burdens.**
Not seeking attention but doing the work. Expanding access to affordable health care. Investing in public schools. Defending the idea that government, at its best, is not distant but present, steady and accountable to the people it serves.
It is the kind of leadership that rarely makes noise, but over time, it leaves a mark.
Right now, there are those who want to take North Carolina – and our country – in a different direction. They see division as a strategy; they mistake power for purpose. They are organized. They are well-funded by dark-money and special-interest groups.
**The only way we can defeat them is if dedicated, caring people like you choose not to sit back but to take part. The power rests in our hands, and we must use it.**

name: Adam Hamilton
subject: “Somebody has to do something”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
Why not me? Why not you?
Friends, I entered this race and hope to enter the Senate with one guiding principle: _What is best for the people of my state?_ Let me backtrack a bit and explain how we got to this point.
**_How we got here_**
Like many great ideas, this one started at home with my wife, LaVon.
Countless times over the last two years I have looked at what is happening in Washington and thought, _this is wrong._ This is not how our country is supposed to work. And it’s not a Republican thing or a Democrat thing; I believe _all of us_ care about decency and humanity. _No one_ is rooting for higher gas and grocery prices or people getting kicked off their health insurance.
The difference is that this time, LaVon responded, **“Maybe _you’re_ the somebody. Maybe _you_ need to do something.”**
**_How it’s going_**
It’s been a whirlwind since we launched this campaign. We went from zero to 60 very quickly thanks to a grassroots team that has shown incredible commitment.
The very same day I became the official Democratic Senate nominee, a new super PAC formed with the sole purpose of opposing me. They quickly went live with attack ads and have spent over $7 million so far.
But there was good news too. National election forecasters like The Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball upgraded our chances of winning, moving Kansas out of the “Safe Republican” category in their rankings. Real Clear Polling shifted us from “Likely R” to “Leans R.” Nate Silver shifted the race in our direction. Even Fox News took notice and moved this race in our direction.
**_What’s next?_**
I’m not going to pretend winning will be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are. The next 30 days will be busy, exhausting and expensive. If there’s one thing I’ve learned in my few months of running for office, it’s that running a campaign takes A LOT of resources (and winning will take even more).

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: After a while that message starts to sink in.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
When a school goes underfunded year after year, it says something. So does a grocery store where the food is barely edible. A tap with water you cannot drink.
These things tell people: “You do not matter.” After a while that message starts to sink in.
And so each and every one of us must tell ourselves the opposite: That we deserve dignity and we deserve respect. Because we deserve policies that put working people first.
Universal child care. Medicare for All. The minimum wage must be a living wage. Our tax dollars should not be spent on bombs and wars abroad. They should be spent on our schools, our bridges, and our roads.
But we are not going to win and make progress on these issues by running the same old campaigns. Power must be put in the hands of everyday people and organizers. Not consultants, not the elite, not pollsters.
In 2018 we won, together, through organizing and building a movement of working class voices that went unheard in our politics for far too long.
Now, over these next 30 days, I am going to be out organizing and rallying with candidates I believe in, everywhere I can, to win the midterms and make real progress on issues like Medicare for All, universal child care, a living wage, and more.
[ If you are with me in this fight, please make a donation of $5 to help our campaign hit the road this fall and win power for all of us by taking back the House and Senate.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20261004.pcHWzL&refcode=em20261004-12396-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12396%2E2526796%2EFc1CKk)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20261004.pcHWzL&refcode=em20261004-12396-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=12396%2E2526796%2EFc1CKk)**
No matter what — whether you can donate today or not — thank you so much for being here.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20261004.pcHWzL&refcode=em20261004-12396-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=1&akid=12396%2E2526796%2EFc1CKk)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20261004-12396-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=2&akid=12396%2E2526796%2EFc1CKk)**

name: Angie Nixon
subject: Big news! 🩷

body:
We need your support to flip this seat back to the people.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261004-1&t=1&akid=4100%2E587540%2ElQd7T5)
Hey Peter,
Angie Nixon here — Democratic Nominee for U.S. Senate in Florida.
**I’ve got some exciting news to share: Leaders We Deserve has officially endorsed our campaign! 🩷 **
We’ve got a lot of work ahead, and I’m grateful for David Hogg and the whole LWD team putting their support behind our fight. LWD only backs candidates who are running real, people-powered campaigns. That’s _exactly_ what we’ve built here in Florida, and it means everything to have them in this fight with us.
**[Big money and corporations can’t buy this seat, and I need us to keep proving it. If you’re all in, please split a $5 contribution between my campaign and Leaders We Deserve now to help us keep doing the work.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261004_1_angie.yitY8O&refcode=em20261004-4100&amount=5&t=2&akid=4100%2E587540%2ElQd7T5)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261004_1_angie.yitY8O&amount=5&refcode=em20261004-4100&t=3&akid=4100%2E587540%2ElQd7T5)**
Now, I wanted to tell y’all a little bit about me.
My mom worked two jobs just to keep food on our table. She was a union member, and she’s the one who taught me what solidarity actually looks like, long before I ever ran for anything.
I’ve spent my whole life fighting for the families in Jacksonville who are one emergency away from losing everything, the kids who deserve a real shot no matter their zip code, and the Floridians who've been told for years that this state isn’t worth fighting for.
A few weeks ago, we proved them wrong. We were outspent nearly 16:1 by the establishment backed opponent — and we won anyway. We did it the old-fashioned way, by talking to the people. And we’re not finished yet. I’ll be out on the doors every weekend between now and November, **because when working people organize, we win.**
Now I'm taking on Ashley Moody, who was never elected to this seat. She was handed it by Ron DeSantis. She's spent her career protecting power. I've spent mine building it, block by block, family by family, right here in the community that raised me.
I’m running to continue that fight in the Senate. For universal healthcare, for a $25 minimum wage, and for a Florida where working people come before corporations _every single time._
**Peter, this fight is personal for me — but I can’t do this without you, and I’m not going to pretend otherwise. Every movement I’ve been a part of has been won by working people ready to lock arms and push back, and this time is no different.**
This is a real fight for the soul of Florida, and I need every person who believes in the work we’re doing together to show up for me right now. I don’t take a dime of corporate money, and neither does Leaders We Deserve. That means this campaign runs on people-powered support, or it doesn’t run at all.
**[Will you split a $5 contribution between my campaign and Leaders We Deserve today to help me flip this seat back to the people?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261004_1_angie.yitY8O&refcode=em20261004-4100&amount=5&t=4&akid=4100%2E587540%2ElQd7T5)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261004_1_angie.yitY8O&amount=5&refcode=em20261004-4100&t=23&akid=4100%2E587540%2ElQd7T5)**
Thank you for riding with us.
Let's win this,
Angie Nixon
Democratic Nominee for U.S. Senate Florida

This is not simply a vague plan or empty threat. Trump has a signed, operational, classified presidential order. It is unreviewed by Congress or any court. And it gives him the legal framework to declare an emergency, label Democratic protesters domestic terrorists, deploy ICE detention infrastructure against American citizens, and challenge certified election results before any court can intervene: | == | The Brennan Center for Justice confirmed it. Keep Our Republic confirmed it. The New York Times reported it. This is why Unpack Our Courts cannot wait. The court that made Trump untouchable sides with him 80% of the time. The network that built that court is already seizing voter records in eight states. His insurrectionists are on a $1.8 billion taxpayer retainer. The coup is already unfolding. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1918, German Chancellor Max von Baden, appointed by Kaiser Wilhelm II three days earlier, [sent a telegraph to President Woodrow Wilson](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAUBOCnMZ2RbbywFC5uQ7e3TYmMfYCT9Q-yTxbx9tFGeYMUU33SaDQfj_lhMWDa_tsIhtY8JzhrACIos9vBPeuaSwSPzhY4CkT8inVWQvVcCi70bB3hC2ZtG29WAAVdA0YOo5TirgbV7Gbw67hI5_wo3aC8F3JYVSe7XskBvNMNmnefFEK_08n2vnS98kuv77fRL7eRaQEeKZf2M2OiHdZw5ReU1uXYBLMTHZV1_5iamJrO82x3rJTL9XamJtqxcm8vjon_ClNTdpQXKFwzNW1Qok0XJwiwFXvslR8FKnpIxE8MNSdeAZ6YNm5LxErooCnGHyeGgLUfmBZbtBh-JtEfn3wZ9R0AAP__7I2MDg) in Washington, D.C., requesting an armistice with the Allied powers in World War I. Yoo-hoo, the wholesome chocolate milk drink that isn't quite chocolate milk, has enjoyed decades of success. In today's _[Whatever Happened To...](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dlu6zAYBODTUJ2Fn5uWgsUDHlwEcJoUKQkuvyzapGlQlAT79IFyhRTTzABfMd8XfTEhhsf10yRUdcr6gfsSsVYs2s3o7suUS0IfnCn4LJjCmhbNgHUnCicQ2rgaNtTCNF5NiAx5g4r2I6UwsJ41s5KjgR5GARaplSNS4B30zFM5wCC9b4I6PAogjnDaDpZ3zNtODHL0Vo5EAPpQc2lvOTzqjFN85Q1L63JqopprfS6E_yPsTNh53_f2lde6Wjz2ozHVzYSfN8L_f3y93-m-4k1CU5R_7iHGsHQ9EXBNJsRfsv7xiU2xnwAAAP__R9px7Q)_ section, we learn that the product has remarkable staying power. In case you missed it on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla counted down the seven pets linked to longer lives. One study that followed 3.4 million people over 12 years found that owners of a particular pet were 40% less likely to die during that period, and it's not the one you'd guess. Some surprising animals made the cut, and the pet that landed at No. 1 isn't even the most popular choice in American homes. Ayla ran through the full countdown and the research behind each one. ## Seniors To Get Checks for Medicare Part B
President[ ](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFyqzAQheGnEZ2Z1SJjKFTchs63TckIaWU2kRAjySZ--wx5hRSnO_MV_8d9vhsOvD3-m0i6-jRvdJRAtVKe7Ur2q_iUIzm2JtOeKfIzlhkB-4uEC6jZ2MovmpVpnPZESF1DWt5GKWHAGzarhn6QV-i9H5TputGhsuANIsoFRgDVsD49CaDOdbIdlq5Ht_RquI5uuY5CATmuKbefibe6kg_v9KLc2hSboNda9yK6fwIngdNxHK1P38uz8EalnB-BkzWVHim_BU4ubSa4S83PuDdZu_3gELj0N6HgEQ2HX7b-scZL408AAAD__42UdIQ)Trump announced on Friday that his administration would begin sending [$90 checks to more than 20 million seniors](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtypDAQRb8GMlGNYHgECjYhm003pPRohl7rQUnNYP-9a-zyFzi42a1b95x_9_WuyVN8_NUBFW9pjXgVj8yYV7ujfStbygEdWZ3xyBjoDGWVIAfRgoB-1ZbpiWuva6c2RIldjaod57aFSY6y3hXqwXSzdnNrcILZbhua6WbAyX4EC1CTeu21AP0rXdtMphukM0M_3WZnbnPVAzrilJv_iSLvuPmP9MTc2BRqr3bmo1Tdn0oulVyu62q29G7OQhFLeXUquRzJE5MtlVw4n-EQOsZ0RotFzCC-SUVIGQXvOgoJQRSMlHIRO_pD2BSMZvFjQthUuNRZueMi76kMY9XDI2jyX6f4ly6fSn4GAAD__0aFjJQ) to help offset the cost of Medicare Part B premiums. A White House fact sheet said the money will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, with most eligible recipients receiving the payments [by direct deposit in early October.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO8yAQRp8GdxPhMb4VFH9Dl7_d0nJgiNnlYgFOlLdfeVd5gi2mGunoO-fjulxX5128_18DyWrTEulZPNVKedEb6a9iUw5knF4z7ZmCO0JZkOMALQcullVX96BFrI2Rlgipa0i249y2fMIRm032ndHjQHrSVpOwhP04TYSWi6EfudGNkyev5Vyc17WX6dYNaG6DmPrZ3PqZCU7G1ZQvn8nFupH1r_SgfNEpNF5ute6Fdf8YKoYqvvZU6vliqE4wQ9Vyhop3DNVR4DRkqGo-wg5rjOmImgrMHH6FwaYMyCE4712K8EzRULaHh0LRpVygJtjI76DPEfCuA-88DFWTpdmfJ6AMIxP8Hlbnf-bWP1Z-SPwOAAD__1jEkr4) In 2026, the [standard Medicare Part B monthly premium](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-O4yAYBPCnwR0WfMbYLiiucZdrr7T48xFzC8ECYmvffpVIeYItpp3Rb_7dtpsOMTzuf3VC1XzeHnjViK1h2eyO9qv6XBK6YHXBo2AKz1Q3YCApZ5SJTdsWTtyE7pzyiIBDh4pPC-dshgm6XbkRBjFIB9xNgrnZIphFe8-kkX6coAvq1ccZE68MvJ_NIMEZKeZxcWZciGDoQsul_5_Do-3o43c-sfQ2py6qvbWjkuEPgZXAel1Xb1Pt7_kksL44JedEYPXaNlp3xFYJrG_CB0YPXVqlhn6E1KF72hZMxNoV5Y4rxBiqnIhg96RDfE-3Xz52KvgJAAD__zUtgZQ) is $202.90, while the annual deductible is $283, according to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. The administration is separately distributing $500 payments to nearly 1 million Americans who purchased health insurance through the Affordable Care Act, claiming the Biden administration overcharged on user fees.
## Man Learns Birth Father is Music Legend

**Whatever happened to Yoo-hoo?** For decades, the [little brown bottle with the yellow label](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykj72OtCAYRq8GujHwiqgFxdfYzdduSfh5GdkFMchq5u437i1s8VRPzknOx1M_TUxxe_03GVULRW94HQlbw6rdiu7rCKVm9NGZinvFHL_zoYGBfHD2YEIb1-KJWhjqVUAE7CkqPs6cswlGoKviVjpr0PJJsuBA4CACB8flMDs3j5ZGdfs4Y-Jez7vJ9hK8lWIaZm-HmQiGPrZSu88St7ZiSO9yYu1cyTSptbX9IP0_AguB5bqu7l3KYy3l_gkstCq_XzGleMiRCPbKJqZftv0x-VTwEwAA__9Y5mry) was everywhere: corner stores, vending machines, Little League dugouts, school lunchboxes. Yoo-hoo was the chocolate drink that tasted like chocolate milk without actually being chocolate milk, and millions of American kids never thought twice about the difference. New Jersey grocery store owner Natale Olivieri created the drink in 1928 after watching his wife boil jars of homemade tomato sauce. He figured the same heat-and-seal trick could keep a chocolate drink from spoiling on the shelf. It worked. By the 1950s, Yankees legend Yogi Berra [was appearing in TV ads](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtuhDAYBODTmG6RX2BTuIgUrdJs2iQV8uNncWKvkfkB7e0jcoUU08xIXzEft_FmY4qP-7vNYHAq4wOONQEi1NHP4H_WqdQMIXpbYamQ45bXkVPeXxi9UDlaj3GHUdommAmAg2jAMDUwRjVXvJnNYC1VXHaSTlyAlpo5NVHducC1Cmpoojk9Rqk8I1irneh5cL3U3RBcNxBJIUQstf0u8YEzTOlZdqitL7lJZkZcViJeCL8Sfj2Oo32WDTcH5342Fv1MxHUn4vUT3Zb8l3_zsqkmLEdMKa69IpLes43pj8R_PrEb_hsAAP__gmVyKw), visiting the factory floor in Carlstadt, New Jersey, and eventually becoming a company vice president. His teammates, reportedly including Mickey Mantle and Whitey Ford, pitched in too, and the Yankees promoted it as "the drink of champions." Pepsi tried to knock off Yoo-hoo off in 1966 with a rival called Devil Shake, but discovered Yoo-hoo held exclusive rights to the sterilization equipment it needed. Pepsi reportedly lost about $5 million and sold the whole operation to Yoo-hoo for $1. Meanwhile, the Yoo-hoo ads just kept rolling out, like this [animated commercial from the 1970s](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dlu6zAYBODTUJ2Fn5uWgsUDHlwEcJoUKQkuvyzapGlQlAT79IFyhRTTzABfMd8XfTEhhsf10yRUdcr6gfsSsVYs2s3o7suUS0IfnCn4LJjCmhbNgHUnCicQ2rgaNtTCNF5NiAx5g4r2I6UwsJ41s5KjgR5GARaplSNS4B30zFM5wCC9b4I6PAogjnDaDpZ3zNtODHL0Vo5EAPpQc2lvOTzqjFN85Q1L63JqopprfS6E_yPsTNh53_f2lde6Wjz2ozHVzYSfN8L_f3y93-m-4k1CU5R_7iHGsHQ9EXBNJsRfsv7xiU2xnwAAAP__R9px7Q). The drink hit its cultural peak in the 1990s, when it became a fixture of gas station coolers and after-school snacking alongside Dunkaroos and Capri Sun. _Seinfeld_ cemented its place in pop culture in 1992 when Brian Doyle-Murray's sad-sack Yoo-hoo truck driver told Jerry, "It's a fine product." Today Yoo-hoo still sits on shelves at Walmart, Kroger, and Amazon, now owned by Keurig Dr Pepper. It technically [contains no liquid milk](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykj72OtCAYRq8GujHwiqgFxdfYzdduSfh5GdkFMchq5u437i1s8VRPzknOx1M_TUxxe_03GVULRW94HQlbw6rdiu7rCKVm9NGZinvFHL_zoYGBfHD2YEIb1-KJWhjqVUAE7CkqPs6cswlGoKviVjpr0PJJsuBA4CACB8flMDs3j5ZGdfs4Y-Jez7vJ9hK8lWIaZm-HmQiGPrZSu88St7ZiSO9yYu1cyTSptbX9IP0_AguB5bqu7l3KYy3l_gkstCq_XzGleMiRCPbKJqZftv0x-VTwEwAA__9Y5mry), just whey, dry milk, and a lot of high-fructose corn syrup.

Its biggest recent move is a Ghost-branded protein drink collaboration that sold out online in 20 minutes. The bottle has changed, but the nostalgia hasn't. _Did you grow up drinking Yoo-hoo? What do you remember about it? Let us know by replying to this email._

Yoo-hoo was the chocolate drink that tasted like chocolate milk without actually being chocolate milk, and millions of American kids never thought twice about the difference. New Jersey grocery store owner Natale Olivieri created the drink in 1928 after watching his wife boil jars of homemade tomato sauce. He figured the same heat-and-seal trick could keep a chocolate drink from spoiling on the shelf. It worked. By the 1950s, Yankees legend Yogi Berra , visiting the factory floor in Carlstadt, New Jersey, and eventually becoming a company vice president. Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

| | | |

| | | Friend,

Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241101%2E444211%2EEaRXmI)
One more day to get registered to vote in Texas. When we started the Every Campus Counts Tour in Arlington back in August, the goal was to go to every major college campus to meet, register and turn out the young Texans who have the power to decide this election.
I've been on the road every week since, and our volunteers have been with me every step of the way.
We've reached more voters this year than in 2024 and 2025 combined and we’re still going, because we know that this is the work that works.
In 2024, 79% of the young voters in our network cast a ballot, compared to 39% statewide.
When we meet someone, register them, and personally stay in touch with them, they show up. That's why I'm heading back out on the road. I'll be in San Antonio, San Marcos, El Paso, Lubbock and Austin this coming week to join our volunteers as we turnout the margin of victory in Texas.

subject: Goodbye
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2049%2E1086043%2EtdzlsT)
This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign for the final 30 days of this election.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261004-1.nRvpaC&refcode=em-20261004-1&t=2&akid=2049%2E1086043%2EtdzlsT)**
After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed.
When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. **I was not on a path to success.**
There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets.
After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland _and the first Black governor in the history of my state._
What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me.
**It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success.**
Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement.
I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today.
That includes the **Maryland Corps and Service Year Option** — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career.
We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. **[If you support that mission, I would appreciate a donation to keep me in the fight as Maryland's governor today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261004-1.nRvpaC&refcode=em-20261004-1&t=3&akid=2049%2E1086043%2EtdzlsT)**
Elevate,
Wes

I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets. After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland and the first Black governor in the history of my state. What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me. It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success. Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement. I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today. That includes the Maryland Corps and Service Year Option — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career. We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. ## Judge Halts Big Bend Border Construction
A federal judge in El Paso on Friday [blocked border barrier construction across the Big Bend region](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFutDAQBOCnMR3Ia8zZFC7-hu7-NiVa8BocGXzCe8fl7SOSR0g_mtE3H_fxjjHFffmPGzl-hzzudJZEzHSMn0-_0IqJy5QPT8eJKRletzwqqW41yFrqEWeOLxo1Vt5N0vdQkQPTAwCYtqtWN5neajBh7jprOqWsneebMapVEq2nvoruqgMpNYBU0DZhxjagJtDtZIMloSX5yPloeCWmN5aQvvKLjmbOW5Xcyvwoov0n1CDUcJ5nE_Lb4LNw3K-IUMOlEmqY4lJPtPv6F1RfovqBz0K-Opx_nDGlWG5GaLlsGNPPAP_1mJdT3wEAAP__aXB5Dg) while a lawsuit against the Trump administration plays out. U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone's order covers the [roughly 500-mile Big Bend sector](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1upTAQhZ_GdL7yGMJPQbGNu2y7JRrsAWZjMLLnXpK3X5F9hHQjjXTOd74_79M7cuRj_Y07jfK5pOmgq0QSoTz9fYaVNoxS5pQD5Qtj7GTb02SNbTUYbZoJvfCLpgarMM4mDFDRCN0AANDVb9U2DkNre2PAowlz179R65HaZmh7QugRKh7vODCmATAW6sfisV6wIWjquV96Uo2hwJLyQzYS-sSyxK_0ovzwaa_iuImcRdW_lHXKuuu6Hh8F5X4q6-49yrozRRb293m3KevAKOuMVdYtFChj1D49s2ih_UwZM8cvPcfkP4qW_NxPjWHng4tkFE6H_u9E31I0H_qbS8-86pmOoDOtnA5lXZXHcF4cI5e2U41Zd-T4DS4_Ff4a7b8AAAD__-Szl-I), including Big Bend National Park and privately owned land upriver and downriver. She found the challengers likely to win on at least one claim. The Center for Biological Diversity, Friends of the Ruidosa Church, and a river guide sued in April, arguing DHS [improperly waived environmental laws](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2S4yAQhU-DMlz8jWQHBJuQzaYbqlrQSMxgcEFL9t5-S94jTPyqX7_v-_M5f0LKqay_4Y6WXrHOBZ89IxG2-WsPK26QqS-1BWxPyHmi7V5nJdTIpeDCzOApHTgbGIJdRLjJAa2cblJKOemPYbM-jDfw6KWPZtR6WoS_xlEFuInJfGgzJHvWSSGMlEJJfYkedASD0ujlGq_IjMCQqLYLbUj4gh7z33pgu_h6H7LdiB6d6V9MOabc95HgDJhyJwtTDjN_QK9MufMRU04KppxQTLmIARtk_kbla4NCnafytRdPqRZOlT9g78iXtPIFS-AFzgDOyvbN_4vhC7SWsHFfS6e2v2-ZckOz4fFMOac-TsyI9Q4pv0fTT2UfVv0LAAD__2X6ljI) such as the Endangered Species Act to speed construction. A CBP construction pause had expired Sept. 30. "_We stand by our assessment and remain confident in our legal authorities to secure the border while preserving the unique landscape of the Big Bend region_ ," DHS said in a statement, adding that it's [working with the Justice Department on next steps](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO2zAQBNCvobo1uBRt2QWLNOoubUphSS4l5ijToDaS7-8DXT4h9QCDefPrY_qgXPJz_kkrO3mnOj352AqLcJt-_4kzL1Rk87VFbgeVMsiy1slocwPUoO1EQfLOk6UuOq_jAzt2ODwQEYf-2i0ODV5v3l5DoCGQfdiHTYE93tDGaMK9y-6sQ60tojbYX1KgPpFltL2_pzsrqzlmqe0iCwu_aUvlq-7cLqGuXXGLyGtT_Q9lRmXGz1Tfsp-RMuOpUWYsNVBRZkwcuVGBbxkcnOdlA-H1VRu1LzitIBV8nsHzM8I_N3hqLXODo7ZPIAEu8KKtwsLU8nPumouvI5eSt9ugrJ5XyuV7m_zvp7szfwMAAP__CwOPxA).

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

I'm Mai Vang — a Justice Democrats-endorsed candidate for Congress in
California's 7th District, a daughter of Hmong refugees, and a Sacramento
City Councilmember who's spent my life fighting for working families.

We've created a little tradition on our campaign.

At canvass launches, house parties, or before our volunteers head out to
knock doors, I call out two words: "OUR TIME!"

And the room calls back: "MAI TIME!"

It started as a small thing, but it's come to mean everything to me — a
reminder that this campaign is about all of us, and what we can do when
working people decide to organize.

So you can imagine what it meant when the primary winners of the Justice
Democrats slate — Chris Rabb, Melat Kiros, Claire Valdez, Adam Hamaway,
Darializa Avila Chevalier, and Donavan McKinney — came together to say the
same thing: that it's Mai Time.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261004-mv.Dz_uVL&refcode=em20261004-38325&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38325%2E1203867%2EnVCGFl ]Tweet by Justice Democrats: We’re sending 7 new members to Congress in
January. And they all want @MaiForUs there with them. Help her beat a
billionaire: maiforus.com/donate

These are candidates who all won their own fights against the
establishment. Every one of them ran the kind of race I'm running —
refusing corporate money, running unapologetically on Medicare for All, on
ending the genocide in Gaza, and on taking on the billionaire class.

And by staying true to those values, every single one of them won.

I'm up next, and this is the toughest race left on the board. I'm facing a
21-year incumbent with a corporate super PAC already spending hundreds of
thousands of dollars to tear us down. The establishment is desperate for
this slate's winning streak to end with me.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261004-mv.Dz_uVL&refcode=em20261004-38325&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=38325%2E1203867%2EnVCGFl ]Every one of these fighters has crossed the finish line — and with your
help, I'll join them in Washington in January. Will you split a
contribution of $10 between my campaign and Justice
Democrats to help us get this done next month?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261004-mv.Dz_uVL&refcode=em20261004-38325&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1022&akid=38325%2E1203867%2EnVCGFl ]Contribute $10

With heart and hustle,

Mai Vang

U.S. Sen. name: Lieutenant Colonel Alex Vindman, US Army, Retired
subject: The Washington Post
body:
Peter: A little more than six years ago, I retired from active military service.
I had no intention to resign from a career I loved, having served for more than 21 years in uniform. But it became clear that Donald Trump had a vendetta against me, and that he would do everything in his power to punish me for speaking truth to power.
On that first day of retirement, I wrote an article in _The Washington Post_ discussing the need to have public servants with the moral courage to protect our democracy. This is more relevant than ever.
I’ve attached the op-ed below. It's an important reminder of why doing what's right matters. Thank you for taking a few minutes to read it.
Before you go, please make a donation to my brother Eugene's re-election to Congress.
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em260925-av&refcode2=1145_3892029_cNb_dp&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp)**
* * *

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em260925-av&refcode2=1145_3892029_cNb_dp&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp)
**Alexander Vindman: Coming forward ended my career. I still believe doing what’s right matters.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em260925-av&refcode2=1145_3892029_cNb_dp&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp)
After 21 years, six months and 10 days of active military service, I am now a civilian. I made the difficult decision to retire because a campaign of bullying, intimidation and retaliation by President Trump and his allies forever limited the progression of my military career.
This experience has been painful, but I am not alone in this ignominious fate. The circumstances of my departure might have been more public, yet they are little different from those of dozens of other lifelong public servants who have left this administration with their integrity intact but their careers irreparably harmed.
A year ago, having served the nation in uniform in positions of critical importance, I was on the cusp of a career-topping promotion to colonel. A year ago, unknown to me, my concerns over the president’s conduct and the president’s efforts to undermine the very foundations of our democracy were precipitating tremors that would ultimately shake loose the facade of good governance and publicly expose the corruption of the Trump administration.
At no point in my career or life have I felt our nation’s values under greater threat and in more peril than at this moment. Our national government during the past few years has been more reminiscent of the authoritarian regime my family fled more than 40 years ago than the country I have devoted my life to serving.
Our citizens are being subjected to the same kinds of attacks tyrants launch against their critics and political opponents. Those who choose loyalty to American values and allegiance to the Constitution over devotion to a mendacious president and his enablers are punished. The president recklessly downplayed the threat of the pandemic even as it swept through our country. The economic collapse that followed highlighted the growing income disparities in our society. Millions are grieving the loss of loved ones and many more have lost their livelihoods while the president publicly bemoans his approval ratings.
There is another way.
During my testimony in the House impeachment inquiry, I reassured my father, who experienced Soviet authoritarianism firsthand, saying, “Do not worry, I will be fine for telling the truth.” Despite Trump’s retaliation, I stand by that conviction. Even as I experience the low of ending my military career, I have also experienced the loving support of tens of thousands of Americans. Theirs is a chorus of hope that drowns out the spurious attacks of a disreputable man and his sycophants.
Since the struggle for our nation’s independence, America has been a union of purpose: a union born from the belief that although each individual is the pilot of their own destiny, when we come together, we change the world. We are stronger as a woven rope than as unbound threads.
America has thrived because citizens have been willing to contribute their voices and shed their blood to challenge injustice and protect the nation. It is in keeping with that history of service that, at this moment, I feel the burden to advocate for my values and an enormous urgency to act.
Despite some personal turmoil, I remain hopeful for the future for both my family and for our nation. Impeachment exposed Trump’s corruption, but the confluence of a pandemic, a financial crisis and the stoking of societal divisions has roused the soul of the American people. A groundswell is building that will issue a mandate to reject hate and bigotry and a return to the ideals that set the United States apart from the rest of the world. I look forward to contributing to that effort.
In retirement from the Army, I will continue to defend my nation. I will demand accountability of our leadership and call for leaders of moral courage and public servants of integrity. I will speak about the attacks on our national security. I will advocate for policies and strategies that will keep our nation safe and strong against internal and external threats. I will promote public service and exalt the contribution that service brings to all areas of society.
The 23-year-old me who was commissioned in December 1998 could never have imagined the opportunities and experiences I have had. I joined the military to serve the country that sheltered my family’s escape from authoritarianism, and yet the privilege has been all mine.
When I was asked why I had the confidence to tell my father not to worry about my testimony, my response was, “Congressman, because this is America. This is the country I have served and defended, that all my brothers have served, and here, right matters.”
To this day, despite everything that has happened, I continue to believe in the American Dream. I believe that in America, right matters. I want to help ensure that right matters for all Americans.

👋 Wait! Before you scroll away...🇺🇸
My brother Eugene won one of the closest House races in the country last cycle, and that makes him a big time target for Republicans who want to keep control of the House, and a president who'd love to defeat the second Vindman twin.
Eugene has a big FEC fundraising deadline coming up in a few days. And when it ends, he's got some difficult budget decisions to make about the rest of the campaign and what it takes to win.
He tells me that he's a bit short of where he needs to be right now, so I was hoping people who care about holding the House could help.
**If $15 seems worth it to you to take back the House majority, then I am asking: Please contribute to my brother Eugene Vindman’s campaign today.**
**[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-oct26?refcode=em260925-av&refcode2=1145_3892029_cNb_dp&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp)**

Paid for by the Alex Vindman Victory Fund, a joint fundraising committee authorized by Alex Vindman for Florida, the Democratic Executive Committee of Florida and the DSCC.
4611 S University Drive #194
Davie, FL 33328
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Small-dollar donations from people like you are the primary way Alex Vindman funds this campaign — if you would like to make a contribution, you can do so by [clicking this link](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em_footer&t=1&refcode2=1145_3892029_cNb_dp&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp).
Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you. If you would like to recieve fewer emails, [sign up here](https://act.alexvindman.com/signup/avfl_feweremails/?t=2&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp) or if you must, you can [unsubscribe here](https://act.alexvindman.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=3&akid=1145%2E3892029%2EcNb_dp).
Alexander Vindman is a former member of the United States Army. Use of his military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the U.S. Army, the Department of Defense or any branch of the U.S. government.

Happy Sunday. We're getting close to the mid-terms and I was thinking that a shot of faith and hope could be just what the doctor ordered. This [excellent book](https://substack.com/redirect/46b8a3c1-33f6-4642-92a8-bc46c516a8fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has been on my mind because I teach it at this point in the semester during my "Faith and Democracy" class at Duquesne University's Thomas R. Kline School of Law. My review of it below is free, then there are some updates for paid subscribers which you can access by becoming a paid subscriber.

What sets _A Stone of Hope_ apart from the huge library of civil rights books is Chappell's argument that the civil rights movement succeeded primarily because of religion. Secular liberals accomplished nothing major on civil rights in the 30s, 40s, and 50s, despite their great power. Even the ones who truly cared couldn't make civil rights "move" as an issue. The southern Black activists, of which King became a surprise leader, made it "move" because their Christian faith gave them courage, and it made them willing to sacrifice.
Chappell is not the only person who has made that observation, but he takes it a step further by showing the entire worldview that allowed these people to make lasting political change. It's a challenge to us, in some ways. Because it's not just that King and his followers were churchgoers who knew scripture. Any of us could copy that if we felt it would give us some special power. What was distinct about them, and much more difficult to emulate, was their understanding and acceptance of original sin. Because of what they and their ancestors had lived through, they were pessimistic about human nature, and therefore about what could be accomplished in this world. Here is Chappell explaining his title:
> In his famous "I Have a Dream" speech at the Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C., in 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. said that he was going back to the South with faith that his people could hew "a stone of hope" from "a mountain of despair." That image captures the philosophy of the civil rights movement. . . . Despair was the mountain. Hope was by comparison small, hard to come by.
Ironically, this made them better political operators than people who had a lot more optimism about what politics could achieve. My students struggle with this irony-- each semester I get papers that say basically, "Things are gradually getting better and the civil rights movement is an example of that." Of course, if things are getting better, none of us need to feel a special obligation to contribute. It's an excuse for inaction.
Chappell shows that, in the case of civil rights, the reason things got better was that _**King and the others knew that things are not "getting better" in a general, historical way; in fact, things usually don't get better**_. But they believed God had set a specific challenge before them, and there was no option to quit.
The passage quoted below gives you a sense of the cost. It comes from King's account of the famous "moment in the kitchen" when he received a late-night phone call threatening the lives of his wife and newborn daughter. He was just 27 years old:
> I got out of bed and began to walk the floor . . . . I was ready to give up. With my cup of coffee sitting untouched before me I tried to think of a way to move out of the picture without appearing a coward. In this state of exhaustion, when my courage had all but gone, I decided to take my problem to God. With my head in my hands, I bowed over the kitchen table and prayed aloud. The words I spoke to God that midnight are still in my memory. "I am here taking a stand for what I believe is right. But now I am afraid. The people are looking to me for leadership, and if I stand before them without strength and courage, they too will falter. I am at the end of my powers. I have nothing left. I've come to a point where I can't face it alone."
> At that moment I experienced the presence of the Divine as I had never experienced Him before. It seemed as though I could hear the quiet assurance of an inner voice saying: "Stand up for righteousness, stand up for truth; and God will be at your side forever." Almost at once my fears began to go. My uncertainty disappeared. I was ready to face anything.
Experiences like this went far beyond King and the other clerical leaders. Chappell has a whole chapter on the experiences of conversion and ecstasy that happened among the rank and file, making it more like a religious revival at times than a political movement. In this sense they were similar to how we think of the evangelical right today -- they believed God was on their side. And "like the Hebrew Prophets . . . . [t]hey had to try to force an unwilling world to abandon sin--in this case, 'the sin of segregation.'" So they engaged in a public form of hating the sin and loving the sinner -- loving him enough to try to change him.
In recent years I've heard political activists express resentment that circumstances forced them to become active. I wish I could have recommended this book to them, because one of the main messages that comes through is what King called "a spiritual discipline against resentment." He believed in something that modern activists also seem to hesitant to embrace: that unearned suffering is redemptive. King knew that he himself was a sinner in need of redemption, and instead of holding him back, that belief helped him keep going.
What lessons does this book hold for us today? In a way, everyone who cares about basic American ideals and values is suffering. It's nothing like the suffering of the subjects of Chappell's book, but it is damaging to see our most fundamental beliefs betrayed and rejected each day. There is so little accountability, and many have given into the temptation to accept that this is the way things are now. That acceptance gives rise to two opposite tendencies, both dangerous: the tendency to withdraw from politics altogether (e.g. people follow the news [much less closely ](https://substack.com/redirect/4005823b-25dd-4724-b5cf-35d1cbcac296?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) now than they used to), or the tendency to "fight" by adopting a posture of moral superiority that is basically uncompromising. It's hard for me to see much of a future in either of these.
If you're able to read this book, the texture of the lives and thoughts of its subjects will suggest a fundamentally different path. Today they would neither back down, nor lose sight of the importance of incremental gains and taking a broad view of who our neighbor really is. ...
