It's a challenge to us, in some ways. Because it's not just that King and his followers were churchgoers who knew scripture. Any of us could copy that if we felt it would give us some special power. What was distinct about them, and much more difficult to emulate, was their understanding and acceptance of original sin. Because of what they and their ancestors had lived through, they were pessimistic about human nature, and therefore about what could be accomplished in this world. Here is Chappell explaining his title: In his famous "I Have a Dream" speech at the Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C., in 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. said that he was going back to the South with faith that his people could hew "a stone of hope" from "a mountain of despair." That image captures the philosophy of the civil rights movement. . . . Despair was the mountain. Hope was by comparison small, hard to come by. Ironically, this made them better political operators than people who had a lot more optimism about what politics could achieve. My students struggle with this irony-- each semester I get papers that say basically, "Things are gradually getting better and the civil rights movement is an example of that." Of course, if things are getting better, none of us need to feel a special obligation to contribute. It's an excuse for inaction. Chappell shows that, in the case of civil rights, the reason things got better was that King and the others knew that things are not "getting better" in a general, historical way; in fact, things usually don't get better. But they believed God had set a specific challenge before them, and there was no option to quit. The passage quoted below gives you a sense of the cost. It comes from King's account of the famous "moment in the kitchen" when he received a late-night phone call threatening the lives of his wife and newborn daughter. He was just 27 years old: I got out of bed and began to walk the floor . . . . I was ready to give up. With my cup of coffee sitting untouched before me I tried to think of a way to move out of the picture without appearing a coward. In this state of exhaustion, when my courage had all but gone, I decided to take my problem to God. With my head in my hands, I bowed over the kitchen table and prayed aloud. The words I spoke to God that midnight are still in my memory. "I am here taking a stand for what I believe is right. But now I am afraid. The people are looking to me for leadership, and if I stand before them without strength and courage, they too will falter. I am at the end of my powers. I have nothing left. I've come to a point where I can't face it alone." At that moment I experienced the presence of the Divine as I had never experienced Him before. It seemed as though I could hear the quiet assurance of an inner voice saying: "Stand up for righteousness, stand up for truth; and God will be at your side forever." Almost at once my fears began to go. My uncertainty disappeared. I was ready to face anything. Experiences like this went far beyond King and the other clerical leaders. Chappell has a whole chapter on the experiences of conversion and ecstasy that happened among the rank and file, making it more like a religious revival at times than a political movement. In this sense they were similar to how we think of the evangelical right today -- they believed God was on their side. And "like the Hebrew Prophets . . . . [t]hey had to try to force an unwilling world to abandon sin--in this case, 'the sin of segregation.'" So they engaged in a public form of hating the sin and loving the sinner -- loving him enough to try to change him. In recent years I've heard political activists express resentment that circumstances forced them to become active. I wish I could have recommended this book to them, because one of the main messages that comes through is what King called "a spiritual discipline against resentment." He believed in something that modern activists also seem to hesitant to embrace: that unearned suffering is redemptive. King knew that he himself was a sinner in need of redemption, and instead of holding him back, that belief helped him keep going. What lessons does this book hold for us today? In a way, everyone who cares about basic American ideals and values is suffering. It's nothing like the suffering of the subjects of Chappell's book, but it is damaging to see our most fundamental beliefs betrayed and rejected each day. There is so little accountability, and many have given into the temptation to accept that this is the way things are now. That acceptance gives rise to two opposite tendencies, both dangerous: the tendency to withdraw from politics altogether (e.g. people follow the news now than they used to), or the tendency to "fight" by adopting a posture of moral superiority that is basically uncompromising. It's hard for me to see much of a future in either of these. If you're able to read this book, the texture of the lives and thoughts of its subjects will suggest a fundamentally different path. Today they would neither back down, nor lose sight of the importance of incremental gains and taking a broad view of who our neighbor really is. ... Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star Autonomous Warfare Command, nicknamed AutoWarCom, to speed the military’s acquisition of drones and artificial intelligence. ---
| | [](https://us.list-manage.com/_mjzfP9SCgr?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)September was filled with noteworthy developments. The Fed raised rates, shattering hopes for the housing markets. AI safety grabbed global headlines. The United Nations met and successfully achieved....well, nothing. The Iran War continued, and diesel prices became front page news. Oh, and I almost forgot, government bond yields marched higher around the world.
See below for links to my thoughts about these (and other) topics as well as a speech I gave at the Freedom Summit are below...
Best wishes for a thought-provoking October!_**

| | **SEPTEMBER 6, 2026**

The dream of almost every immigrant who arrives on our shores is that they will be measured not by their past or their parents’ professions but instead by their own ability. And more importantly, perhaps, that the next generation will grow up in a land of opportunity. Indeed, for generations, the goal of most parents (immigrant or not) was for their children to have it better than they did.
The path chosen to achieve this goal was almost always education. Many parents (mine included) prioritized education over almost every other activity. Time and money were dedicated to schooling and support for learning. And more often than not, the system worked. Many children of immigrant households found themselves entering elite schools and finding opportunities their parents never imagined.
I am living proof that it was possible for immigrants to come here, work hard, encourage and prioritize education for their children, and to see their children enjoy better lives. But this bargain rested on an assumption nobody really had to examine, at least not until today. We knew what that an education was valuable, distinguishing, and would retain its worth indefinitely. I am no longer confident in my last sentence...

| | **SEPTEMBER 13, 2026**

Every generation has a defining moment, one they carry with them for the rest of their lives. The one where time stops, the world changes, and all teens and adults remember where they were the moment they heard the news. These events tend to split time in a way that we thereafter demarcate life as before or after it. For our grandparents, it was Pearl Harbor. For our parents, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. For our generation, it was the terrorist attacks of 9/11. And everyone remembers where they were.
For me, I was in Washington D.C. I was supposed to fly back to Boston on the morning of September 11, but my then-fiancée (and now wife), still at Harvard Law School, asked if I might be able to come back a bit early to help with some wedding planning. So I changed my flights and returned on Monday September 10th. I recall flying through a thunderstorm with jarring turbulence. And on 9/11, I was at my desk when I heard the news. Friends and family, who knew I was supposed to be flying, called to check on me.
And while in shock watching the news unfold on TV, I still remember being paralyzed with panic after learning that one of my friends had departed Logan to attend meetings in Los Angeles. A few hours later, his spouse and I shared a moment of sheer joy when we learned his boss, a very wealthy man, had insisted my friend connect...

| | **SEPTEMBER 20, 2026**

I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don’t run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price just hit [$6.43 a gallon](https://us.list-manage.com/18bl9WBo3TO?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)...the highest price ever recorded in the United States.
That’s not just a number I read in a headline. It’s a number I see embedded on every invoice, every cost sheet, and every freight bill that crosses my desk. And that’s probably true for most manufacturers. Inputs arrive by trucks run on diesel. Outputs depart by trucks running on diesel. And it’s a number that is quietly raising the price of everything you buy...

| | **SEPTEMBER 27, 2026**

Regular readers of _Navigating Uncertainty_ know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn’t worked.

Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that’s killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world’s biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can’t have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn’t address state-sponsored intellectual property theft?
Just this week, US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei delivered comments at the United Nations General Assembly describing the death of...

The one where time stops, the world changes, and all teens and adults remember where they were the moment they heard the news. These events tend to split time in a way that we thereafter demarcate life as before or after it. For our grandparents, it was Pearl Harbor. For our parents, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. For our generation, it was the terrorist attacks of 9/11. And everyone remembers where they were. For me, I was in Washington D.C. I was supposed to fly back to Boston on the morning of September 11, but my then-fiancée (and now wife), still at Harvard Law School, asked if I might be able to come back a bit early to help with some wedding planning. So I changed my flights and returned on Monday September 10th. I recall flying through a thunderstorm with jarring turbulence. And on 9/11, I was at my desk when I heard the news. Friends and family, who knew I was supposed to be flying, called to check on me. And while in shock watching the news unfold on TV, I still remember being paralyzed with panic after learning that one of my friends had departed Logan to attend meetings in Los Angeles. A few hours later, his spouse and I shared a moment of sheer joy when we learned his boss, a very wealthy man, had insisted my friend connect... | | | | SEPTEMBER 20, 2026 I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don’t run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price just hit highest price ever recorded in the United States. That’s not just a number I read in a headline. It’s a number I see embedded on every invoice, every cost sheet, and every freight bill that crosses my desk. And that’s probably true for most manufacturers. Inputs arrive by trucks run on diesel. Outputs depart by trucks running on diesel. And it’s a number that is quietly raising the price of everything you buy... | | | | SEPTEMBER 27, 2026 Regular readers of Navigating Uncertainty know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn’t worked. Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that’s killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world’s biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can’t have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn’t address state-sponsored intellectual property theft? Just this week, US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei delivered comments at the United Nations General Assembly describing the death of... | | | | | EXCLUSIVE SUBSCRIBER CONTENT: Vikram’s Speech - Freedom Summit | | | | | 2026-2031 Predictions | | | | Read Vikram’s Prior Predictions! | | Since 2015, Dr. Mansharamani has publicly posted a set of global developments to watch over the following five years. Corporate executives, government leaders (including several heads of state!), journalists, academics, and others eagerly read, reread, and look forward to his annual piece. If you reread his prior pieces, you’ll find some developments he noted come to fruition, and others simply did not happen. But as Dr. Mansharamani repeatedly notes, the goal of the predictions is not accuracy , but instead usefulness in provoking thoughts about possible futures. Click on the link below to review his posts from 2015 through 2025. | | | | NAVIGATING UNCERTAINTY | | As many of you are aware, I’ve returned to writing my weekly newsletter and have been pleased by the rapidly growing interest in my thoughts. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Need to turn this around fast, Peter
body:
I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1591&source=&t=1&akid=4228%2E124072%2Er_WU71) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
My team was going through our supporter records, and we noticed how yours stood out from the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that _I know_ how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it.
**Today, I’m asking you to take the next step. Here's why:**
Grassroots fundraising has slowed down recently, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have already been pouring just shy of $100 million so far into North Carolina to defeat me, and now, President Trump's super PAC has unleashed millions more to double down on their attacks.
We need to turn this around fast – and the first step is getting our fundraising back on track. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us reach this week’s goal? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1591&amount=5&t=8&akid=4228%2E124072%2Er_WU71)
North Carolina is the best chance Democrats have to flip one of the four seats we need to take back the Senate, so if we lose here, we lose our shot at flipping the majority. The only way we’ll avoid that is by building the resources to compete with the massive amounts of GOP spending.
**Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you, giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
_With less than a month to go until Election Day, Peter, I need you._
[**_Time’s running out, so I’m personally asking: Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to my campaign today so we can flip North Carolina’s critical seat and help Democrats secure the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1591&amount=5&t=9&akid=4228%2E124072%2Er_WU71)

name: Gina Hinojosa
body:
The New York Times last polled our race 3 months ago and found us down 7. This poll has swung 10 points since then.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&refcode=em20261004-2324&amount=5&t=1&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)
In June, the _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.
**Today, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. **[Chip in $5 right now to help us turn this polling lead into a win.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&refcode=em20261004-2324&amount=5&t=2&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)**
The _New York Times_ also ran a major story yesterday on the state of play in Texas. Read this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&refcode=em20261004-2324&amount=5&t=3&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)
**Ten-to-one. Abbott has thrown everything he has at this race, and he still can't put it away.**
Wendy Davis put it this way in the same article: "People have vastly underestimated Gina. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen."
That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. **[Will you make your first contribution today to help us keep our momentum going in the final stretch?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&refcode=em20261004-2324&amount=5&t=5&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)**
The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am.
Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. **Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it.** Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way.
We are 30 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. What happens next depends on whether we have the financial resources to communicate our message to the voters who need to hear it.
**[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us reach every voter in every corner of Texas and defeat Greg Abbott on November 3rd?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&refcode=em20261004-2324&amount=5&t=6&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_nyt.PBrWwo&amount=5&refcode=em20261004-2324&t=25&akid=2324%2E299639%2EL1jlHI)
For 32 years, Texans have been told a Democrat can't win statewide. A 10-point swing after more than $70 million in spending against us says otherwise. Let's go take Texas back.
Thank you — for everything,
Gina

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3338%2E259176%2EGEY7Yq) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3338%2E259176%2EGEY7Yq)_

Dear Peter, I want to tell you about someone who’s unbelievably great. Someone who understands what’s at stake in this moment, who listens, who leads, and who embodies the values that make Minnesota, well, _Minnesotan._ That person is Peggy Flanagan. And she’s running to represent our great state in the U.S. Senate. [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17724?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.04_Flanagan-Powwow_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=4&akid=3338%2E259176%2EGEY7Yq) I’ve known Peggy for a long time. We both grew up in St. Louis Park (not at the same time — she’s young, and I’m old). Raised by a single mom, Peggy knows the impact of federal programs that help working families. They had a home because of a Section 8 housing voucher. Other public programs helped her mom afford health insurance and child care. **She gets it because she’s lived it.** And that’s exactly the kind of leader we need in Washington. (And frankly, what we have way too little of.) | | [ELECT PEGGY TO THE SENATE >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17725?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.04_Flanagan-Powwow_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=5&akid=3338%2E259176%2EGEY7Yq)
---
Peggy’s got the experience, too. She’s currently serving as Minnesota’s Lieutenant Governor — the highest-ranking Native American woman ever elected to executive office in the U.S. Before that, she was a state legislator, a school board member, an executive director for the Children’s Defense Fund–Minnesota, she even worked for ME!
But most importantly — she worked for my friend and hero, the late Senator Paul Wellstone. She and I both believe in his guiding principle: _We all do better when we all do better._ (Yes, it’s that simple. No, Republicans still don’t get it.)
While Republicans are hiding from their constituents, Peggy is doing the opposite. She’s traveling the state hosting ‘Kitchen Table Conversations’ — actually listening to _real_ Minnesotans, having real conversations, and working to bring people together. She doesn't just want to fight against bad stuff. She wants to build something, too.
Oh, and in case you’re wondering — yes, Peggy will be the first Native American woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate. It’s about time. She is Ojibwe and a member of White Earth, and her Anishinaabe name, Gizhiiwewidamookwe, means ‘speaks in a loud and clear voice woman.’ If there’s one thing I know about Peggy, it’s that she’ll use that voice to fight for all Minnesotans — whether they agree with her or not.
[**So let’s make it happen. Split a donation with Blue Amp Action today, and help send Peggy Flanagan to the Senate, where she’ll keep speaking up, fighting hard, and making sure we all have a good hotdish recipe.**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17725?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.04_Flanagan-Powwow_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=6&akid=3338%2E259176%2EGEY7Yq)

name: Citizens for Amanda Pusczek
subject: The final stretch
body:
We have less than a month to turn out the voters who will decide this race.
---
| | | | | |
---
| | | Friend,
Election Day is less than a month away, and every single decision we make between now and then counts.
As a nurse, I’ve spent my career working directly with families who are pushed to the brink by rising costs—people forced to choose between groceries, rent, and life-saving prescription drugs. Working families across Alabama’s 4th District deserve real representation in Washington that fights to lower everyday expenses and serves as an uncompromising check on corruption and political overreach.
Pundits love to write off our state, but you and I know the truth: **Alabama isn’t a red state—it’s a non-voting state.**
Decades of neglect and uncontested races have told hundreds of thousands of our neighbors that their voices don’t matter. When we actually organize, knock on doors, and show up with a message focused on healthcare, accountability, and kitchen-table stability, people listen.
We can build a truly competitive campaign here, but organizing across our communities requires real resources. From yard signs and gas money to direct voter outreach tools, we have to fund every last push ourselves.
**This is the final fundraising email you will receive from me before Election Day.**
To keep our organizers equipped and reach our key voter targets across AL-04, we need to close the gap on our critical $10,000 October goal before the clock runs out.

---

Mass deportation and efforts to push millions of people out of status are already costing each taxpayer an average of **$2,358 a year**.2 **[Working people are being treated as disposable by those in the highest seats of power. Children were kept home from school, our neighborhoods were turned into militarized zones, and our neighbors disappeared from our streets and workplaces. More than 340 DACA recipients have been detained and more than 90 deported, as far as we know. More than 100,000 children, most of them U.S. citizens, have been separated from their parents. More agents means more neighbors snatched from our communities without due process and more families torn apart. **Citizenship is the only solution to the chaos and instability that mass delegalization is creating.** It would also mean a $4,300 raise for millions of workers in the first five years.2 **[Congress found more than $100 billion for enforcement. | [](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDRfSVMtQ1QuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQzMzg3LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA0X0lTLUNULjExMDExN190MjA0MzM4Ny0yMDY4In0/ObqB8SPJE0HWj-iNnRBeZw)
---
That’s a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a “girl power” kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more “feminine,” but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn’t use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the “Blossom” stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that’s not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I’m going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some “master” in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I’m asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMDRfSVMtQ1QuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDQzMzg3LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDA0X0lTLUNULjExMDExN190MjA0MzM4Ny0yMDY4In0/5-sqrg5A84N0u27v-9xxnA)
Because I’m a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.

**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home. I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country. After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents. Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence. But silence costs more. So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue. I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first. Election Day is just over four weeks away, and some of the most important races in the country could come down to a few thousand votes.
#
Hi there,
Election Day is just over four weeks away, and some of the most important swing races in the country could come down to a few thousand votes.
When margins are as close as we expect in Swing Left target districts and states, the conversations volunteers have with voters on the doors and on the phones can decisively shape the midterm election outcome and our work to shift the national balance of power.
**That’s why we’re working to hire 3 new Ground Truth organizers in these final few weeks, and we need your help to do it!**
We’re working to hire organizers in states that are make-or-break for our path to the Senate: Alaska, Texas, and Maine. And these organizers won’t be knocking doors alone. Each Ground Truth organizer will recruit and train volunteers and lead canvasses where dozens of members of the Swing Left community will come together to have conversations with voters in the final days leading up to November 3rd.
But time is short, and every day it takes to fill these roles is a day of canvassing we can’t get back.
[**That’s why we’re asking you to make a donation of $25, or any amount you can, to help hire 3 new Ground Truth organizers for the final sprint toward Election Day.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl.QSDeHu&refcode=em20261004-2996&amount=25&t=2&akid=2996%2E1562180%2EA6k8nr)

[_**Here's my question, Derek: what should Democrats be focused on in the final 30 days before Election Day?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140631048/651109230/734443882?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_FinalPriorities_261004_T1_1&ms=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_FinalPriorities_261004_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGM5MmM0ZC0wNGMwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QVzg7sbJkx_LvXA2jJOOqQ5CkQizN3bizCEFnnkLj68=&emci=2442b84f-91be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=e0c92c4d-04c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=4568237) **[SHARE YOUR PRIORITIES](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140631051/651109233/734443882?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_FinalPriorities_261004_T1_1&ms=MW_ATA_EM_SVY_FinalPriorities_261004_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMGM5MmM0ZC0wNGMwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QVzg7sbJkx_LvXA2jJOOqQ5CkQizN3bizCEFnnkLj68=&emci=2442b84f-91be-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=e0c92c4d-04c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=4568237)** Folks like you, Derek, who've powered this campaign by showing up, speaking up, and pitching in, are the ones I most want to hear from as my campaign shapes our strategy for the final four weeks.

name: Jeff Bridges
subject: 64 counties. No copy-and-paste solutions.
body:
There’s really no substitute for standing on someone's front porch and hearing what’s on their mind. You learn things you simply can't from polls.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9932665ab770/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379200?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/saHQec891ec?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Sunday started with breakfast at Fitch Ranch Cafe in Granby, then coffee at Simple Coffee in Fraser. Excellent food and coffee, go if you get the chance.
I joined Phil Weiser, Joe Neguse, and a room full of volunteers ready to knock doors for Liz Newsom, Democratic candidate for Clerk and Recorder. Then headed out to the doors.
**There’s really no substitute for standing on someone's front porch and hearing what’s on their mind. You learn things you simply can't learn from polls. You get the texture behind our cost-of-living crisis.**
---
|
---
| | In Fraser, that means hearing how a world-class ski resort just down the road creates jobs and opportunity, while also pushing housing further out of reach for the folks who live and work there. And how local governments can help—or hurt.
After a morning of conversations in Grand County, we hopped back in the car and headed to Clear Creek County for a rally on Main Street with local Democrats.
---
|
---
| | **What Fraser and Idaho Springs have in common with every other place I've visited across our state is a cost-of-living crisis. But we can't solve it with one answer copied and pasted into all 64 counties. The headline may be the same. The particulars aren't.**
---
|
---
| | That’s one of my favorite parts of running statewide. You start to see that the problem may be shared, but the devil and the divine are in the details.
Understanding what's actually happening requires showing up, knocking doors, and listening. More towns. More doors. More conversations.
More miles ahead.

---
| | Talk soon,
ps If you haven’t had the chance to go leaf peeping yet, make plans to do so this weekend. The colors were already peak Colorado!
---

Friend of Life, It's easy to assume that God measures our lives the way the world does. After all, we're constantly surrounded by messages telling us to accomplish more, earn more, influence more, and become more. Success is usually measured by what people can see...In Scripture, we see something entirely different. Again and again, God reminds us that He is looking for faithfulness. When Jesus told the parable of the talents, He didn't praise the servant who had the most abilities or the greatest opportunities. He commended the servants who were faithful with what had been entrusted to them. That truth has encouraged us many times at PreBorn!. Most of us will never be famous. We may never write a book that reaches millions, preach to a packed stadium, or lead a large ministry. But every one of us has opportunities each day to be faithful. Opportunities to love our families well, to serve our churches, to encourage someone who's hurting, to share the hope of Christ, and to use the gifts God has given us for His glory. Those moments may seem ordinary, but Scripture reminds us that they are anything but ordinary. They are part of a life that echoes into eternity. That's why we've created a free devotional called _[Hearing Jesus Say, "Well Done."](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLuO3SAQhp8Gdz7iZnxcUESxLKXYSGk2JWJhsJG4CbDP60feZF8g3Wj-T99cfr-pN-2DT_tPHUGay6valNO-H-4MCVrz7XXoHnXvUJuimIqR4BFzpU33FyiuByuNFYwOIMm8EELFwsRwyNk5xp-C04kzPjGiCRfCutkymMVTuMHLW0cw5mQiE30-4MNg7GbB3DJxvTjE8Vms7tAeJqcG9dL3TJ9SvqucHibHIcij99IQ-4bohuhWoeWzGmiPUuEj108K0e0FIYw2JxgLYtvZo_rLIbaWmlsB033aERV3FMH6MyK2QtQ-_GsaHYv2e0JsvWW36yvJqUPqiK3vRP2ax-_vP8av44YqbXn5EHwTM-J4v42fm_f_fPgl6Z8AAAD__-UokxE)_ Over the course of ten days, you'll spend time in God's Word reflecting on what it means to live faithfully, steward your life well, and keep eternity in view. Each day includes Scripture, biblical teaching, guided prayer, and reflection questions to help you apply these truths to your own walk with Christ. Our prayer is that this devotional encourages you to keep following Jesus faithfully--one day, one decision, and one opportunity at a time. clean_body: That truth has encouraged us many times at PreBorn!. | | | | Friend of Life, It's easy to assume that God measures our lives the way the world does. After all, we're constantly surrounded by messages telling us to accomplish more, earn more, influence more, and become more. Success is usually measured by what people can see...In Scripture, we see something entirely different. Again and again, God reminds us that He is looking for faithfulness. When Jesus told the parable of the talents, He didn't praise the servant who had the most abilities or the greatest opportunities. He commended the servants who were faithful with what had been entrusted to them. That truth has encouraged us many times at PreBorn!. Most of us will never be famous. We may never write a book that reaches millions, preach to a packed stadium, or lead a large ministry. But every one of us has opportunities each day to be faithful. Opportunities to love our families well, to serve our churches, to encourage someone who's hurting, to share the hope of Christ, and to use the gifts God has given us for His glory. Those moments may seem ordinary, but Scripture reminds us that they are anything but ordinary. They are part of a life that echoes into eternity. That's why we've created a free devotional called Over the course of ten days, you'll spend time in God's Word reflecting on what it means to live faithfully, steward your life well, and keep eternity in view. Each day includes Scripture, biblical teaching, guided prayer, and reflection questions to help you apply these truths to your own walk with Christ. Our prayer is that this devotional encourages you to keep following Jesus faithfully--one day, one decision, and one opportunity at a time. Thank you for allowing PreBorn! to encourage you in your faith. In Christ, The PreBorn! Team Pop Acta Media | Conservative Innovation PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 |

Folks, it’s James Carville.

I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:

**For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.**

We wait until a race becomes a crisis.

We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.

We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.

Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.

Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.

He founded [**Equal Opportunity Now**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140634596/651119678/1090555623?refcode=261004_carville_resend&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODNiOWZhNy0wN2MwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oLNsnj9TkqIowV6PP7IFOEFrzEALIn-lTPqkVcQSxGg=) to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.

And all I can say is:

**FINALLY.**

Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.

But Raja cannot build this by himself.

[**Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140634597/651119679/1090555623?refcode=261004_carville_resend&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODNiOWZhNy0wN2MwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oLNsnj9TkqIowV6PP7IFOEFrzEALIn-lTPqkVcQSxGg=)

Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
**Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.**
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.

Peter, Before I came home to Illinois, I was a meteorologist at a local station in Tyler, Texas. One morning, my boss approached me and said we needed to speak after the show. When I got to the conference room, I saw my employment contract laid out on the desk. Next to it was a printout of my profile from a gay dating website. I was told I had a choice: to be _"that person"_ in the profile or _"have a job."_ I decided then and there to resign and move back to Illinois. **That was more than 20 years ago, and the reason I’m sharing this story now is because I never imagined the LGBTQ community would be experiencing such a surge in discrimination since Trump and his allies – like my opponent – came back into the picture.** We've seen another round of far-right politicians hoping to shrink us from public view, and scrubbing entire histories off government websites. In case it ever needs saying, these people have never been the good guys. I can tell you for a fact that if I were a kid today watching this, I'd be feeling scared, isolated, and ashamed, as so many groups are right now. So you can imagine how I felt when I saw that my opponent, Dillan Vancil, said it was "making everything political" when I asked friends to not support organizations funded by people whose mission is to send LGBTQ people back into hiding and out of public life. Think about that: _Fighting for our right to exist is too “political” for someone who wants to represent us._ **These tone deaf comments are a reminder of why we need representatives in Congress who can lead with empathy – especially when it comes to protecting youth who may already feel marginalized.** [**I’m standing up to hate in Congress, but it's going to take a team effort to get this done. The Trump administration thinks there’s nothing “controversial” about ICE’s violent behavior, terror tactics, and disregard for human rights and human life.

Friend — most people would say that 58 deaths under the watch of the US government are 58 too many.
But apparently, the Trump administration thinks there’s nothing “controversial” about ICE’s violent behavior, terror tactics, and disregard for human rights and human life.
**Give us a break.**
The fact of the matter is that the Trump administration is holding tens of thousands of people in ICE detention centers across the country in intentionally cruel, inhumane, and deadly conditions.
Inadequate food and water, medical neglect and lack of access to health care, cramped and over-crowded cells and holding areas, unsanitary conditions, hard concrete for sleeping, mold and insect infestations, and limited access to legal counsel have become the status quo.
Many of the people stuck in these detention centers are legal residents, visa-holders, asylum-seekers, refugees, or even US citizens — folks who were following the law and still found themselves being held in detention by this administration for the sake of cruelty and intimidation alone.
And to make matters worse, every new detention center is a money-making opportunity for for-profit prison companies.**The whole thing is morally repugnant.**
Make no mistake, we are being ruled by cruel, heartless people who have completely trashed our American values of compassion, justice, and fairness. We have an obligation to defeat the MAGA far-right for the sake of the very soul and future of this country.

My office is already getting reports of it: mail about your voter registration or whether you can vote that doesn't come from any official source. Groups that send this kind of mail often use outdated or wrong information about voters. That's no accident. Confusion is the whole point.**I won't pretend we know yet who's behind every one of these mailers. But we know the playbook, and it's the same one we've watched all year.** **First,** Donald Trump tried to use an executive order to control who gets a ballot through the Postal Service. In a state that votes entirely by mail, that could have frozen our elections. Oregon fought back, and the Supreme Court shut him down 7–2. **Now** the attacks are coming quietly: out-of-state callers pushing false election information, and mail meant to make you doubt whether you're registered or whether your ballot counts.**It's always the same goal.** If Trump and his dark-money allies can't change the rules, they'll try to make you give up on the system before you ever vote. **Here's how to beat it. Real election mail carries the official logo, with the stars and stripes, the words "Official Election Mail," and "Authorized by the U.S. Postal Service." If you're unsure, check your registration at oregonvotes.gov or call your county clerk.** Oregonians trust vote-by-mail because it works, and I'm not going to let anyone scare people out of it. But fighting disinformation takes resources: getting accurate information to voters, answering every lie quickly, and standing up to Republicans who want to rig this system for themselves. **[Can you chip in $10 right now to my campaign so we can amplify this information and fight back against these election games?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140636193/651122932/-569431239?refcode=261004-fake&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYjU1N2Q5OS0wOWMwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q4xL994ZfriySVzlS5qMn3-1HNchJ2RSfxBsQrw89U8=)**

clean_body: | | | = | | | Misleading election mail is already landing in Oregonians' mailboxes. = My office is already getting reports of it: mail about your voter registration or whether you can vote that doesn't come from any official source. Groups that send this kind of mail often use outdated or wrong information about voters. That's no accident. Confusion is the whole point.I won't pretend we know yet who's behind every one of these mailers. But we know the playbook, and it's the same one we've watched all year. First, Donald Trump tried to use an executive order to control who gets a ballot through the Postal Service. In a state that votes entirely by mail, that could have frozen our elections. Oregon fought back, and the Supreme Court shut him down 7–2. Now the attacks are coming quietly: out-of-state callers pushing false election information, and mail meant to make you doubt whether you're registered or whether your ballot counts.It's always the same goal. If Trump and his dark-money allies can't change the rules, they'll try to make you give up on the system before you ever vote. Here's how to beat it. Real election mail carries the official logo, with the stars and stripes, the words "Official Election Mail," and "Authorized by the U.S. Postal Service." If you're unsure, check your registration at oregonvotes.gov or call your county clerk. Oregonians trust vote-by-mail because it works, and I'm not going to let anyone scare people out of it. name: Beau, Vivienne, & Wilder (Jerri's kids)
subject: Why you should vote for our mom
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Green for Governor
body:
| [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140638241/651126257/-1977837920?refcode=10-04-fromthekids&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83ODg3MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDJmNWE5YS0wYmMwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=9qN9Ua8gA9xx66XNRoWpl5Vr8NBglBqxHbJH3R0nXrg=&emci=041a3644-04c0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=842f5a9a-0bc0-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=53531271)
---
Hey Team, It's _**Beau, Vivienne, and Wilder**_(you know, the kids Jerri Green is _always_ talking about). You might say we're biased, but _we think our mom is pretty incredible..._ **We want to tell you a story about _our mom_. **Last April, she was in the hospital and was in immense pain from an eye injury. When _she could have been resting_ , she had me (Beau) _read out her entire City Council briefing to her. _ **She did this because she cares about Memphis,_and because she cares about Tennessee._** She's the kind of person who will _wake up at 6 AM on a Saturday_ and stand out in 20 degree weather _to hand out water to her constituents during a boil advisory. _ She's the type of person who has raised her kids from the age of four to volunteer, and _always takes us to the polls to remind us how important voting is._ _**We are so lucky to call her mom. **_She's helped _thousands of people i_ n Shelby County, and _we can't wait to see her help many more across our whole state._ **We know our mom is ready to lead because we've seen _how much she cares_ up close. Hi Peter, A new report has found that ectopic pregnancy deaths across the country have nearly doubled since the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_. I wish I could say this is surprising or somehow unexpected, but it really isn't. These women’s deaths were entirely preventable, and the suffering their families have had to endure in the wake of these losses was avoidable. As an OB-GYN, I treated patients with ectopic pregnancies throughout my career. Let me be clear about what an ectopic pregnancy is: it is a medical emergency. A pregnancy that implants outside the uterus can almost never survive, and without immediate, appropriate care, it can rupture, putting the mother’s organs, her future fertility, and her life at risk. There is no version of this that is not a medical crisis requiring urgent intervention. Abortion bans are putting doctors and patients in an impossible position. Providers in red states are forced to delay or withhold care that their patients urgently need, and women are being told to wait until they’re “sick enough” to treat – or worse, they’re not receiving any care at all. And the problem goes deeper than the abortion bans themselves. Trump and Republicans gutted key healthcare research funding, bringing the work of studying maternal health outcomes to a halt. The CDC's division of reproductive health lost most of its 100 employees, and the entire team responsible for monitoring pregnancy-related risk is on paid administrative leave. More women are dying thanks to these attacks on our healthcare, and Trump and Republicans would rather look the other way – and refuse to measure the damage. **So here’s what I do know as an OB-GYN who took care of patients for more than twenty years: Study after study has shown that restricting reproductive healthcare worsens maternal health outcomes. This was predictable, and it happened anyway – because Republicans are choosing ideology over medicine.** **I ran for Congress because I knew the harm these policies would cause. And I am not going to stop fighting until every woman in this country has access to the care she needs.**

clean_body: All because Republicans are choosing ideology over medicine| | | | = Hi Peter, A new report has found that ectopic pregnancy deaths across the country have nearly doubled since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. I wish I could say this is surprising or somehow unexpected, but it really isn't. These women’s deaths were entirely preventable, and the suffering their families have had to endure in the wake of these losses was avoidable. As an OB-GYN, I treated patients with ectopic pregnancies throughout my career. Let me be clear about what an ectopic pregnancy is: it is a medical emergency. A pregnancy that implants outside the uterus can almost never survive, and without immediate, appropriate care, it can rupture, putting the mother’s organs, her future fertility, and her life at risk. There is no version of this that is not a medical crisis requiring urgent intervention. Abortion bans are putting doctors and patients in an impossible position. Providers in red states are forced to delay or withhold care that their patients urgently need, and women are being told to wait until they’re “sick enough” to treat – or worse, they’re not receiving any care at all. And the problem goes deeper than the abortion bans themselves. Trump and Republicans gutted key healthcare research funding, bringing the work of studying maternal health outcomes to a halt. The CDC's division of reproductive health lost most of its 100 employees, and the entire team responsible for monitoring pregnancy-related risk is on paid administrative leave. More women are dying thanks to these attacks on our healthcare, and Trump and Republicans would rather look the other way – and refuse to measure the damage. So here’s what I do know as an OB-GYN who took care of patients for more than twenty years: Study after study has shown that restricting reproductive healthcare worsens maternal health outcomes. This was predictable, and it happened anyway – because Republicans are choosing ideology over medicine. I ran for Congress because I knew the harm these policies would cause. body:

It’s Keisha Lance Bottoms. Usually, I ask engaged supporters like you to chip in $10 or $25.
But this is a critical moment. Nate Silver just downgraded our race in Georgia from Lean D to a complete Toss-Up. My opponents and outside special interest groups are flooding the state with millions in spending, and anything you can spare helps us fight back.
**So I’m lowering my ask. I’m hoping you can chip in just $5 today to my campaign and Aaron Ford:[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_af_20261004_2_ak?refcode=20261004-1000 ](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/86?c0=em_ms_af_20261004_2_ak.xtEQFp&refcode=em20261004-1000&t=2&akid=1000%2E127862%2ET3odtv)**
Just $5 to fight back against the tidal wave of conservative super PAC spending trying to buy Georgia.
Just $5 to keep our ads on the air and keep our organizers on the ground across the entire state.
Just $5 to protect our progress and win an unprecedented victory right here in Georgia.

**[So please, rush a donation of any amount to my campaign and Aaron Ford right now to help me respond:](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261004_2_ak.fbd_sv&amount=5&refcode=em20261004-1000&t=3&akid=1000%2E127862%2ET3odtv)**

Peter,
From Olympic National Park to Mount Rainier – it's no secret why we call Washington the Evergreen State.
**By protecting 2 million acres of our pristine backcountry national forest lands, the Roadless Rule has played a big part in keeping it that way.**
More than just jaw-dropping views, our public lands support local jobs and economies, preserve crucial headwaters and fisheries – including our salmon – sustain Indigenous cultural practices, and shield our communities from wildfire.
But this administration doesn’t care – in fact, its push to reverse the Roadless Rule is just part of a larger pattern of attacks on iconic public lands across the Western United States, including:
* Gutting the Forest Service and National Park Service's budgets and staff,
* Illegally cutting billions set aside for conservation and natural recovery,
* Trying to bulldoze Big Bend for an unannounced border wall extension,
* Attempting to secretly give a parcel of Yosemite to real estate developers (!!) and more.

Like the inflationary tariffs, the health care and food stamp cuts, the mass layoffs, and more, it's just another means to the President's ultimate end: **enriching corporate elites like himself at the expense of hardworking Americans – our outdoor wonders and the planet our kids will inherit be damned.**
But our public lands belong in the _public's_ hands, not just one man's.
So it's on us to take a stand. **And that starts by building grassroots strength to show the GOP that we won’t sit by and let them sell out our pristine national treasures.**

clean_body: I need your help to fight back. | | | = Peter, From Olympic National Park to Mount Rainier – it's no secret why we call Washington the Evergreen State. By protecting 2 million acres of our pristine backcountry national forest lands, the Roadless Rule has played a big part in keeping it that way. More than just jaw-dropping views, our public lands support local jobs and economies, preserve crucial headwaters and fisheries – including our salmon – sustain Indigenous cultural practices, and shield our communities from wildfire. But this administration doesn’t care – in fact, its push to reverse the Roadless Rule is just part of a larger pattern of attacks on iconic public lands across the Western United States, including: Gutting the Forest Service and National Park Service's budgets and staff, Illegally cutting billions set aside for conservation and natural recovery, Trying to bulldoze Big Bend for an unannounced border wall extension, Attempting to secretly give a parcel of Yosemite to real estate developers (!!) and more. Like the inflationary tariffs, the health care and food stamp cuts, the mass layoffs, and more, it's just another means to the President's ultimate end: enriching corporate elites like himself at the expense of hardworking Americans – our outdoor wonders and the planet our kids will inherit be damned. But our public lands belong in the public's hands, not just one man's. So it's on us to take a stand. And that starts by building grassroots strength to show the GOP that we won’t sit by and let them sell out our pristine national treasures. = | | = Thank you for standing with me, Patty | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Too many politicians forget that purpose. They are more focused on chasing flashy headlines or scoring points against the other party than on creating real solutions to improve the lives of those they serve. Our leaders shouldn’t be keeping score. They forget that our government exists to solve problems and build the future, not just referee party interests. People back home worry about paying their bills, putting food on the table, and what their representatives are doing to make their lives easier. They don’t care about abstract policy debates. They don’t want rhetoric; they want results, whether that be affordable housing, functional institutions, opportunities for their children, or simply something to look forward to on the weekend. Politics can and should make those things possible. **Heaven help us if we lose this race.**
Folks, I don't say that lightly.
Nevada families are paying more for rent, groceries, and health care. And all MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo has to tell us is that we should be ready to _"feel a little pain" from Trump's tariffs._
Well, we're feeling it.
I know what it’s like to struggle to make ends meet. I raised my first son as a single dad in college.
That’s why we’ve focused this campaign around lowering costs and supporting working families — and our message is resonating across the state.
**But MAGA billionaires are working overtime to protect Lombardo and his disastrous policies.**
Right now, they have more money to run more TV ads than we do. If we let them continue outpacing us over the airwaves, this race could slip away from us.
That’s why I’m turning to you.
**If we can get our message out to more undecided voters, I know we will defeat Lombardo this November.**
We just need the grassroots resources to get it done. Can you chip in $5 or more to help us keep fighting?

Thank you,
Aaron

**Last Call in Fairfield: Who Picks Up the Tab When a Brewery Leaves**
On February 22, 2026, the last truck rolled out of the Anheuser-Busch brewery on Busch Drive in Fairfield, California, and a fifty-year partnership ended in a corporate press release. Anheuser-Busch came to this corner of Solano County in 1976 because of one thing above all: water. Solano County held some of the plum water rights in the state, fed by Lake Berryessa and carried through the Putah South Canal. A brewery, before it is anything else, is a water company. Anheuser-Busch came for Lake Berryessa the way a miner comes for gold. Now the gold rush is over, and the town is holding the bill.
Here is what Fairfield lost in a single day. A plant that produced roughly 124 million gallons of beer a year. Two hundred to two hundred fifty jobs at the end -- closer to 475 in the good years -- making the brewery the sixth or seventh largest employer in town. Utility fees that helped keep the city budget honest. A name that showed up on youth sports banners and charity checks for five decades. A street literally named Busch Drive. None of it is coming back, and none of it is being replaced.
But the beer itself was only half the story. The other half is what happens to everything the brewery touched every single day -- starting with the water going in and ending with the grain coming out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57c13560-693f-420e-b98a-87d977300ffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The water bill arrives**
The Fairfield brewery drew about 2 million gallons of water per day. That sounds like a lot, and it was: roughly 7 percent of the city's entire water system. Here's the part that doesn't get talked about on business pages. Water infrastructure doesn't flex. Pipes, pumps, treatment capacity, reservoir contracts -- the city built and paid for a system sized to serve a brewery that was there every morning. Those are fixed costs. They don't shrink when a customer leaves. They just get divided by fewer people.
Fairfield's mayor has already warned that water rate hikes are likely. Translation: the 7 percent hole in the system is being plugged by homeowners, on their monthly bills, for years. The brewery used the water for fifty years and paid its share. Now the share gets redistributed to the people left behind. That's not an abstraction. That's a line item on every water bill in a town of about 120,000.
**The $7 million goodbye**
And here is my favorite detail, because it tells you everything about how modern corporations think. In July 2024 -- barely a year before it announced the closure -- Anheuser-Busch put out a press release celebrating a $7 million investment in the Fairfield plant. New roofing. New equipment. Structural repairs, the company said, "to ensure the brewery continues to brew, package and ship for years to come."
Sixteen months later, the place was padlocked.
What happened to the $7 million? Corporate math happened. When a fifty-year-old plant no longer hits margin targets, you face a choice: keep operating and keep bleeding, or walk away and write off the upgrades as a sunk cost. Anheuser-Busch walked. The $7 million became a rounding error in a spreadsheet, and Fairfield became a line that got deleted. Production moved to other plants in other states. Nobody in St. Louis felt it. Everybody in Fairfield did.
This is what efficiency looks like from the inside of the balance sheet. From the outside, it looks like a town being used up. Happy, Gavin?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/69da3c4e-bb6f-4b01-b66b-4e22f1b61a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The ripples: beer, beef, and everything between**
The brewery's departure didn't just remove a factory. It removed a node from a supply chain that ran through the region's farms. Every brewery produces mountains of leftover spent grain, and for fifty years Fairfield's spent grain went to local cattle and dairy ranchers as cheap, reliable feed. That flow has stopped. Ranchers now have to buy feed on the open market, and when feed costs rise, they don't eat that cost (pun intended) -- they pass it down. Higher feed prices mean higher milk prices, higher beef prices. The brewery is gone, and the cow down the road got more expensive.
The beer itself is going up too. Production from Fairfield shifted to other Anheuser-Busch facilities farther from California, and supply chains that ran through Solano County now run longer, slower, and thinner. Analysts expect the disruption to cost consumers another $2 to $3 per case. So the drinker in Sacramento or Reno pays for a decision made in a conference room they'll never see.
Add it up. Ratepayers pay through water bills. Ranchers pay through feed. Drinkers pay through the case price. Two hundred fifty families pay with a livelihood. And the corporation? It absorbed a $7 million write-off -- about the cost of two Super Bowl ads -- and moved on.
**Nobody warns you the well ran dry**
The most sobering part of the Fairfield story is that the closure of the main plant wasn't even the first warning. The company had already hollowed out the site's office and customer operations in earlier rounds of consolidation. The pattern was visible for years: shrink, consolidate, and finally, leave. Towns across America are living the same arc on different timelines -- the refinery, the paper mill, the plant, the distribution center -- each announced with a press release about "modernization" and "efficiency."
Fifty years ago, Anheuser-Busch came to Fairfield because the water was good and the deal was good, and for most of those fifty years, both sides held up their end. The town supplied the water, the workforce, and the loyalty. The company supplied the wages, the fees, and the grain for the cattle. It was a genuine partnership, and it worked.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0f898361-044b-4ffc-a588-68e4f113e303?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The lesson of Fairfield isn't that companies leave. It's that when they leave, their costs don't leave with them. The costs stay. They get soaked up by ratepayers, ranchers, workers, and drinkers -- quietly, bill by bill, case by case -- while the balance sheet that abandoned them closes clean.
Fairfield kept its end of the deal for fifty years. Now the town gets to pay for the privilege. "You're welcome" signed Sacramento
\---
If you live in a town with a plant that's been there longer than you have, ask who owns it, where its headquarters is, and what happens to the water bill when it's gone. The answer is the same everywhere.
\---

**Last Call in Fairfield: Who Picks Up the Tab When a Brewery Leaves**
On February 22, 2026, the last truck rolled out of the Anheuser-Busch brewery on Busch Drive in Fairfield, California, and a fifty-year partnership ended in a corporate press release. Anheuser-Busch came to this corner of Solano County in 1976 because of one thing above all: water. Solano County held some of the plum water rights in the state, fed by Lake Berryessa and carried through the Putah South Canal. A brewery, before it is anything else, is a water company. Anheuser-Busch came for Lake Berryessa the way a miner comes for gold. Now the gold rush is over, and the town is holding the bill.
Here is what Fairfield lost in a single day. A plant that produced roughly 124 million gallons of beer a year. Two hundred to two hundred fifty jobs at the end -- closer to 475 in the good years -- making the brewery the sixth or seventh largest employer in town. Utility fees that helped keep the city budget honest. A name that showed up on youth sports banners and charity checks for five decades. A street literally named Busch Drive. None of it is coming back, and none of it is being replaced.
But the beer itself was only half the story. The other half is what happens to everything the brewery touched every single day -- starting with the water going in and ending with the grain coming out.

From the get-go, the GOP knew we had what it took. Now, it’s time to prove it.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&source=&t=1&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0) | | | |
---
Hey, Peter, it’s Roy. Have you marked your calendars yet?
One month from today, we’ll know the outcome of this election. **And in just 11 days, folks will start casting ballots in person during early voting. I need your help to reach them before then.**
[**_Time’s running out to spread our message and impact the outcome of this race, so I’m personally asking you to pitch in $5 or whatever you can to my campaign today._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&amount=5&t=8&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&amount=5&t=9&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)
---
From the get-go, national Republicans made it clear they were ready to open their wallets and make this one of the most expensive Senate races of the cycle.
14 months and tens of millions of dollars later, they made good on that promise, and it’s no secret as to why:
Experts say our campaign has the juice to flip North Carolina’s U.S. Senate seat blue for the first time since 2008. That’s good news, because we have to win here to have any chance of taking back the Senate majority.
**I've won tough statewide campaigns here in North Carolina before, and the only way I’ll do it again a month from now is if grassroots supporters like you power us to victory.**
So before North Carolinians start heading to early voting sites, we need to be ready. We need to head into these final four weeks with the momentum and resources to take on everything MAGA throws our way.
Hundreds of thousands of folks have contributed already. Now, I’m asking you to join them and know that you’ve done all you can to wake up on Nov. 4 with a Democratic Senate.
[**_So please, will you pitch in whatever fits in your budget – whether it’s $5 or $10 – to help us cross the finish line in North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&amount=5&t=10&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&amount=5&t=11&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&amount=25&t=12&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)
---

Roy Cooper

| |
* * *

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1584&source=&t=3&akid=4176%2E124072%2ElFs4_0)

subject: This race is about three things.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/19931?t=1001&akid=1944%2E181023%2ElEIhBC ][IMG]

Hi there, it’s
Jocelyn Benson.

This race is fundamentally about three things: costs down, wages up, and
ending the corruption that got us here.

I’ll get into the details in a moment, but first I need you to know: I’m
running to make Michiganders’ lives better, not harder, but I’m up against
a billionaire-backed MAGA extremist in one of the most important races in
the country. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/19931?t=1002&akid=1944%2E181023%2ElEIhBC ]With less than a month to go, I’m humbly
asking you to step up today and make your first contribution to our
campaign.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/19931?t=1003&akid=1944%2E181023%2ElEIhBC ]Donate →

Throughout this campaign, I’ve traveled across Michigan, talking directly
with hardworking families, and I keep hearing the same stories.
Michiganders are drowning under the skyrocketing costs of everyday
expenses.

From the grocery store to the gas pump, from the doctor’s office to the
rent bill, far too many families across Michigan are struggling to make
ends meet.

One thing is clear: Michiganders need a governor who cares about making
their lives better.

That kind of leadership can’t be bought by billionaires like Elon Musk and
the DeVos family. It requires running a campaign the right way, asking
voters for their support one conversation at a time, and building
resources one dollar at a time.

That’s the kind of campaign we’re building together. One that’s ready to
fight tooth and nail to make real change for Michigan families.

But first, we must win this November. A movement capable of taking on the
national GOP and an opponent backed by the DeVos family and Elon Musk is
only built by everyone pitching in whatever they can, whenever they can.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/19931?t=1004&akid=1944%2E181023%2ElEIhBC ]With less than a month until Election Day, I’m personally asking you to
please pitch in whatever you can today to help us win one of the most
important governor’s races in the country.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:
