Time is ticking:

We're just under one month out from Election Day, and the pressure is on. But not for the reasons you might think...

The truth is: **I don’t want to let you down.**

_You_ are the heart of this campaign. Since the very beginning, this grassroots team has made it possible to compete with massive spending from special interests. You’ve proven that when working people come together, we can win:
* When Peter Thiel dropped $3.6 million against me in a single week, you helped keep our own ads live.

* When JD Vance personally attacked me, you stood by me and helped this campaign surge ahead.

* And when crypto billionaires decided to put $30 million behind new attack ads spreading lies about me, you helped us fight back.

But this race is far from over.

All eyes are on Ohio, and the money continues to _pour_ in. **In fact, Republican megadonors are spending more here than in Georgia, Alaska, and North Carolina combined. Let that sink in.**

I’m not sharing this to scare you – the polls keep proving that we have what it takes to win – but I’m writing this to remind you just how important you are to this movement.

**In the face of a quarter of a BILLION dollars being spent by Republicans in Ohio, our campaign has been able to stay competitive _only_ because of grassroots donations from folks like you. And right now, I need you to have my back more than ever.**

My past races have taught me that this close to Election Day, resources are what allow a candidate to pull ahead. So we cannot give the GOP an inch.

[**Today, I’m asking you to chip in your first $5 to my campaign. I’m counting on you. Will you give what you can to help us flip Ohio and take back the Senate?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140643897/651145913/-1260785309?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6513&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMTYzNDkyOS0xN2MwLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GfHEXE5FhjHYJXgD1Dysk--phH5jTGhbg7OAawj9Rpk=)

Sherrod Brown

There's nobody fighting for Ohioans in the U.S. Senate right now, and I won't sit on the sidelines while working people get screwed over by large corporations and wealthy political donors.

name: Katie Britt (R-AL)
subject: Friend, see the story that shaped me.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc
body:
From dance classes and a hardware store to the Senate.
|
---
| | | | [](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
---
| | |
---
| | Friend,
My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. **I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be._That’s just not who I am._**

In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran.

I ran because I’m a _**mom**_ , a _**wife**_ , and a _**conservative**_ who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system.

I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down.
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before coming to the Senate, I served as the first female president and CEO of the Business Council of Alabama, and before that, I was Chief of Staff to Senator Richard Shelby. **I’ve never shied away from a challenge—and I’ve never forgotten who I’m fighting for.** In every role I’ve held, my mission has been the same: _deliver real results for Alabama families and the American people._
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before starting my career in public service, I earned my undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Alabama. That experience taught me how to lead, think on my feet, and fight for what I believe in—**and it laid the foundation for _everything_ I’ve done since.**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
But long before that, I was just a small-town girl from Enterprise, Alabama. My dad ran the local hardware store. My mom taught dance to almost every kid in town. We didn’t grow up with wealth or political connections. **We came from hard work, grit, and doing things the right way._That’s how I was raised, and that’s exactly how I lead._**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
My husband Wesley and our two amazing kids are my rock. In 2011, a tornado tore through our home and nearly took our lives. That moment changed everything, and reminded me what truly matters. __**Faith** , **family** , and **resilience**.__
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it.

My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day.

_**_I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country._**_

But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, **and I’m not about to start now.**

The radical Left wants to _silence_ conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm.

I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom.

**The support I’ve received so far means everything, but this fight is far from over.** We need the resources to keep going strong and hold our ground.

**[So, after hearing a bit of my story, will you take a moment to chip in whatever you can afford to help me keep up this fight? The road ahead won’t be easy, but I’ve faced tough battles before. And it would mean the world to have you standing with me.](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)**
|
---
[CHIP IN TO FIGHT WITH KATIE BRITT >>](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Thank you, and may God bless America.

Katie Britt (R-AL)
|
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---

body:
I grew up in inner city Cincinnati, raised by a single mother. At 10, we moved to a farm in Sabina. Here's what I took from both of those places. |
---
Fellow Conservative,

I grew up in inner city Cincinnati, raised by a single mother.

We didn't have a lot. But she made sure I understood something early: nobody was coming to hand me anything. Whatever I was going to build, I was going to have to build it myself. She said it more than once. She meant it every time.

When I was ten years old, our family grew and we moved to Sabina, Ohio. Population: a few thousand. A farm town in Clinton County where people got up before the sun and worked until the job was done. That move changed the way I saw the world.

| [**THIS IS WHERE IT ALL STARTED >>**
](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=e5e90bf0bb0d4469a529757343c7346c&_e=rroIXSNRG34x0UmT2kdXn73NPEWlfC6yeH6Ky-Fq-ku0k7VH2mv9x-bIWyNJ5j9foeq9zmln5-YZt1oRw71H_EozVfxHe-7wPDVRRHZ21KHh7wZo5M3wJaQ0ROH3a0ihKssyd7w7sdbPREwkGLcF6KP53QvdFPECl3jsoj--okz6NstB3xYJt3M70DfvOXyu1W9_JgO9xM6V6tH9Y3JL1WG24o1gPV5s42RlVNQNvMLER7ganmTNxO6Mc2imFGgcQbS-f_wGW1eCd_3GdupVyqdw7DwLkGIiMZAzMx9VNGqIeNEMMDFNGT6gPNMMvWRtmIlH0AwrgEfFz61GdRNdWeU-zm7m2yw3OHVUvrR7ZykhkDrhCcpJsp79ASGNVoiGnQ49nTDCWWQ9KGCisieWtEMylzFMjyEVMW8CQEWWZa54drzgw_AKZuZFZkkIG2HodGxpB_c5Wfj-UXxuUFqmdbiw898J_ShwAWvf5QZJFYGOJdPb9tgk4lQ1kk7XS-CH0eymjcGvQ_FXYTZMIp7HAEL06nrlr_Uv-PPYz1NNu40zngLw-awDY5mfGP10a5yZzUcCmUSGEmUAaN64NFTMBoeV7uGZ_1BUmbBjPr4Wjz7NTsJcn23WvYGeE19Z_iVxiVC6thxdHaGHd-p5hZb9riBvBFuSVCmT4Y9aFiKSFg1dygu1isZoyBeLkuYSkW4U3S2dr02yLWbFwTXsghqiWg%3D%3D)
---

On that farm, I started my own hay-baling business as a kid. Nobody told me to. It was just how things worked out there, you saw a need, you filled it, and you got paid for the work. Simple as that. I carried that lesson into everything that came after.

After high school, I followed a family tradition of service. I earned an ROTC scholarship, attended the Marion Military Institute, and served as an officer in the Army National Guard. The military taught me things you cannot learn in a classroom. Accountability. Discipline. The understanding that the person next to you is counting on you to do your job, and that there is no such thing as a bad day at someone else's expense.

[ ](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=e5e90bf0bb0d4469a529757343c7346c&_e=rroIXSNRG34x0UmT2kdXn73NPEWlfC6yeH6Ky-Fq-ku0k7VH2mv9x-bIWyNJ5j9foeq9zmln5-YZt1oRw71H_EozVfxHe-7wPDVRRHZ21KHh7wZo5M3wJaQ0ROH3a0ihKssyd7w7sdbPREwkGLcF6KP53QvdFPECl3jsoj--okz6NstB3xYJt3M70DfvOXyu1W9_JgO9xM6V6tH9Y3JL1WG24o1gPV5s42RlVNQNvMLER7ganmTNxO6Mc2imFGgcbJJbmyZd4oWe2gP1FlouhRLL02tgTRcE1ubdSBxiwkub2nBjDq_TW7D8Gwmc-2YodMjj4JUzUQL-dq-11FNV_EC3z9q0OBvZiM7_2kyxByn8uA4LS9BhATpnlK4l5UCfjW0nHwVJ0eqfBMA19qOugIF70ANkErtQbSwcRn9Op2CNSX7QWem5vlJb_6L-fggBxCHczvYtfM5w_a-kIFujnCD_LbMFRZ7fwVv53a8yMUd8ZwG0wCT9IiW5_T4KI3-guhAsEetjg53qBfN1agfYunt0RxXD327DM3zCieNA5f0816315X_5upgVtVoT3BU9fzACNDJeIsFcbG50swtfjBiXaMfenTXJA311XA8uSpnQ67o-OwC8cRn--40vyYxQseqIZ2pu5XUEaXXcgpdhjgRUYtQ01XzCFHIPeXoLjWuJd7-K12EgFMeb4PXv4Rngwzp-OEztR3Thug0QaOoGgQ%3D%3D)
[**THE FIGHT THAT BROUGHT ME HERE >>**
](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=e5e90bf0bb0d4469a529757343c7346c&_e=rroIXSNRG34x0UmT2kdXn73NPEWlfC6yeH6Ky-Fq-ku0k7VH2mv9x-bIWyNJ5j9foeq9zmln5-YZt1oRw71H_EozVfxHe-7wPDVRRHZ21KHh7wZo5M3wJaQ0ROH3a0ihKssyd7w7sdbPREwkGLcF6KP53QvdFPECl3jsoj--okz6NstB3xYJt3M70DfvOXyu1W9_JgO9xM6V6tH9Y3JL1WG24o1gPV5s42RlVNQNvMLER7ganmTNxO6Mc2imFGgcGGRI-uKDfBkQIfJSKWuQymXuGENfvlZ-_KDnagDagR0OBoIpYhFx4aXkFhTVNF8haFAlqPJ-uezCWtZ2MKBHMkWYTsZD4OU7kpDNyyqLAUHeDexfp0PpOWIR-HUDS9Rgc5yefKbuhkjIHzBswbgpVaxRFT01RKStY5XxNj49w94nCuekav4Scf3CDZ3YEcgvYBGY0u0IHOcqtE84TyBA72oKoSIP9TbreGpp_1RmAIRBKlM-UUszI0oxaGsp-1yRsDdmUB72UPQQlqMjQ8SCL5lbfAGkt5tn9AGiKkPxGE7ZH7Qr076X0rPNR-ibMpBez79mXW6Azy4HYsxYliwNjAeCF3PzxJi4dZJU06bc3oa16Xxs9_rjTicbeqX9p-tQbQB5lw62N_8UpLbaG7fUn2--FhneaQXNwvatdssAk4IbScUKLeBeqHJXObLmp1LxR0rflnwH8elRISAPUZYoBw%3D%3D)
---

I went on to Ohio State for my degree, and then spent more than twenty years as an energy executive fighting for Ohio coal miners and American energy independence. I watched men who had given their whole lives to this industry get squeezed out by regulations written in offices a thousand miles away by people who had never met them. I fought for their pensions. I fought against the failed energy policies that drove up prices and made American workers pay the bill for Washington's bad decisions.

That fight is what eventually brought me to Congress.

[**THE FIGHT THAT BROUGHT ME HERE >>**
](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=e5e90bf0bb0d4469a529757343c7346c&_e=rroIXSNRG34x0UmT2kdXn73NPEWlfC6yeH6Ky-Fq-ku0k7VH2mv9x-bIWyNJ5j9foeq9zmln5-YZt1oRw71H_EozVfxHe-7wPDVRRHZ21KHh7wZo5M3wJaQ0ROH3a0ihKssyd7w7sdbPREwkGLcF6KP53QvdFPECl3jsoj--okz6NstB3xYJt3M70DfvOXyu1W9_JgO9xM6V6tH9Y3JL1WG24o1gPV5s42RlVNQNvMLER7ganmTNxO6Mc2imFGgc96ax1iwf3nkdqipDzweSHJeQ1JBTXSInO2WkmfH9GR3oP-kytmBToKNvWyB6IVfA84GL2SkWUVaJbLjT6NPXTSBeIps52fK-3oPZ1fJKaZb5MWR3rJORxEmLuy666u1Hl8-FMPQNcX7HtHJ2Kjr-1de7jvLIjb3NS1_u5EhuTUDw0rUH5hZ3jML9pkmid5c1CwBuJZwApKJXsyLRvHjFkOrxy-W1zmpZfe1JIHTNO6Tgg5xm0geFV3GxBPnFKLFSuCQxaTgPph14McWr9F7mYTxKR15WHLXCo8P79rDCUDbuFAPgx8-7cZY3I3XiK7z_c_uZ1G_wTrB3lVHVpIdlU4llhFV2aXoclCAeBaJrG-oSk1mQwO53-Yj4vHy7GXSTyJP97qAUKwTEgCVrHSMhCZ9On5wSw5Ct3U756G20avqae6OAOGCxYx_eTjgF85pOKEF-PleLxXj7w9sJoJPCKw%3D%3D)
---

In 2021, I ran in a special election. I was an outsider. The establishment had a preferred candidate and the money was going somewhere else. But the people of Ohio's 15th District took a chance on a guy from Sabina with no political pedigree and a lot of reasons to fight.

[ _**I have not forgotten that. A farm town in Clinton County where people got up before the sun and worked until the job was done. That move changed the way I saw the world. | On that farm, I started my own hay-baling business as a kid. Nobody told me to. It was just how things worked out there, you saw a need, you filled it, and you got paid for the work. Simple as that. I carried that lesson into everything that came after. After high school, I followed a family tradition of service. I earned an ROTC scholarship, attended the Marion Military Institute, and served as an officer in the Army National Guard. The military taught me things you cannot learn in a classroom. Accountability. Discipline. The understanding that the person next to you is counting on you to do your job, and that there is no such thing as a bad day at someone else's expense. I went on to Ohio State for my degree, and then spent more than twenty years as an energy executive fighting for Ohio coal miners and American energy independence. name: OnePA Team
subject: Weapons contractors cannot buy our government
body:
Demand that the Senate Ethics Committee investigate weapons contractor pay-to-play and hold those involved accountable. | |
---
Peter, Working families are told to accept overcrowded classrooms, hospitals closing, and housing we cannot afford. We organize, show up, and demand investments in our communities. Weapons contractors have another route to public money through campaign checks and access to the politicians deciding where our tax dollars go. **ProPublica has exposed a weapons contractor’s account of trading political donations for Pentagon contracts, implicating Sen. Susan Collins and potentially others.** The reporting, titled, _“The FBI Anti-Corruption Squad Was Circling Susan Collins — Until Trump Got in the Way,”_ raises urgent questions about hundreds of thousands of dollars in allegedly illegal contributions supporting Collins’ 2020 re-election campaign in exchange for tens of millions in government contracts. The contractor gave FBI investigators a 50-page document identifying dozens of lobbyists, congressional staffers, and members of Congress he said helped trade cash for contracts. The Senate must account for who used public office to serve this operation, where our money went, and who must be held responsible. **Trump gutted the FBI anti-corruption teams pursuing the investigation. The Senate Ethics Committee must take up the evidence, investigate Sen. Collins and other senators implicated, and hold anyone who violated Senate rules accountable.** [**Demand that the Senate Ethics Committee investigate Sen. Susan Collins and others implicated in weapons contractor pay-to-play and hold those responsible accountable.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39hylK4L3MZYxYPDe3b9JwX6pRpcHKOtu3mwXNt3PiVTvbgvLomBp1BWlolI3UDEqE63fl2ntJkKlMknDC5_GwWzrjrncVuDFABKlxANkjeQX49nSobuR_RRFCYpIijZd_o5Q17MS5a14Z6lWCxWWdWE8U1h4nLat2Dw9sFcIDHfikXl1FUDVO-yPXIPQ04DZ_RzVoCp1KcwrXdJyujoMrKdn-5HttmE-V4haOCGZLE7flLyg6PUQV7oquhmAq7j6HOBIPPFGG1Yn3thCQoBZLa_CVLZtY2u-ML8947NcXiqZwJwK58d1vwQ7oY7kglRA35d81W8w4553Tom9Ppa1ILVtdDr-AK8u3uULddIUlCD7w85puQ4mN6KTHUkcVDXfaPsU9L24Mbz9h0UtD2FOZdgSUHIi0pb0052VpeElSUTp4SdANSmvFrJBK-cn8HEuw/4ul/nNtE29UxRPmn6vVqEQl47g/h0/h001.d7VcBq3LtAoDt-TFdsW8kNLJbWmgncw11cXe1COdg5E) | | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39hylK4L3MZYxYPDe3b9JwX6pRpcHKOtu3mwXNt3PiVTvbgvLomBp1BWlolI3UDEqE63fl2ntJkKlMknDC5_GwWzrjrncVuDFABKlxANkjeQX49nSobuR_RRFCYpIijZd_o5Q17MS5a14Z6lWCxWWdWE8U1h4nLat2Dw9sFcIDHfikXl1FUDVO-yPXIPQ04DZ9VppoSanQSEeoYgQYNnJ_IKC7GMNMDiutBMMcXMxYKiU4R_55ChmqiFTGwgALGF3VKYtTxCKNQhTv_lB61Y69GwZYZCRiSrcq0pvjqbReY_dLbPbmoC4lanUxvNl1MlZooYTjhs0rW-Zvz9uY3HzwI4yrU_keTiaZjiHC7mYV8-JnKvprCheZWc2ciNhfT8PXZEmTDMYf_ulIRblsuVkT3ZD8NO2xcA0JmHGYfDNdSEk-QpDJOKtOACrylj9D1WmE/4ul/nNtE29UxRPmn6vVqEQl47g/h1/h001.w_uOEW0fIFjc38tLCxNHDuhvHSQ96ebph_fUq_Rg8hc)

**Every dollar directed through these arrangements came from the public. Working people earned that money and paid those taxes. We have every right to demand a full accounting from the lawmakers entrusted with spending it.**
Congress is weighing an enormous increase in Pentagon spending while our communities fight for basic investments. Senators cannot keep handing weapons contractors more public money while leaving these questions unanswered. They must investigate the records, question the people involved, and make their findings public.
OnePA members build power through our relationships with neighbors, the leaders we develop, and the people we organize to hold elected officials accountable. We know that changing who government answers to takes sustained pressure from communities prepared to demand more.

The key to saving the MAGA Movement is Friend!

Wednesday at the Port of Brownsville had all the trappings of a coronation: shovels, cranes, an American flag rigged to a boom like a sail. Vice President JD Vance called Saronic's new shipyard "the American dream renewed." Governor Greg Abbott promised up to 10,000 jobs and -- by his office's estimate -- $264.5 billion in economic impact, one of the largest development projects in Texas history. The banner over the day: "American jobs, American dominance." The renaissance of American shipbuilding is here, the Trump administration says, and Texas will play a leading role in it.
Believe them. Then do the thing a real renaissance should survive: check the numbers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e133e78e-3fee-40e2-859d-fc3c5d79d1b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What Port Alpha actually is matters. Saronic Technologies is an Austin startup that builds autonomous boats and drones -- defense hardware, not container ships for Walmart. The yard will cost $3.2 billion, cover 850 acres (about the size of Central Park, expandable past 4,000), and at opening add 150,000 gross tons of annual shipbuilding capacity -- which the governor's office touts as more than double the country's current shipbuilding capacity. The first phase goes live in 2028. Chew on that: one startup's yard doubles national capacity. That's not a renaissance boast. It's a confession about how small American shipbuilding actually is.
Now the water. Volume is the tide every shipyard has to rise on. What has it done since 2024?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b576a6e0-6268-4513-83ce-fe9b68fd4e67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2024, the major U.S. ports moved 25.5 million TEUs -- twenty-foot containers, the unit shipping counts by. In 2025: 25.4 million, down 0.4 percent. NRF's September 2026 forecast puts 2026 at about 25.7 million. Read that again: _three years, and the line has barely moved_. Zero net growth since 2024 -- while analysts counted 2025 as the biggest year for global container volume ever recorded, and BIMCO's analysts watched U.S. imports sink "while the rest of the world sails ahead."
The monthly ledger is where the _politics_ shows. May 2025, the tariff shock: imports fell 11.4 percent in a single month, China down 20.8. September 2025 brought the steepest monthly drop in years -- down 8.4 percent, with China-origin volume down 22.9 percent year over year and China's share of U.S. imports sliding from 34.5 to 33 percent in one month. October fell 7.5 percent below the year before. January 2026 came in 6.4 percent under January 2025, and the first quarter was forecast down 9 to 17 percent. June 2026 surged 14.3 percent -- but only because June 2025 had been gutted. Ocean contract rates fell last year for the first time since July 2024. Hackett Associates, whose data underlies NRF's tracker, said it plainly: a small decline for 2025 versus 2024, "and a further, larger decline in the first quarter of 2026." The tide didn't collapse in one wave. It stopped rising.
And if the goal was independence from Chinese trade, the value numbers say the tariffs did what they promised: U.S. goods imports from China fell 29.9 percent in 2025 -- $131.7 billion gone in a single year -- and the bilateral deficit dropped 31.8 percent. But here's what nobody put on the podium: total import volume did not grow to replace it. _It went nowhere_. We didn't trade China for Texas. We traded volume for slogans.
This matters because of what the ceremony claimed to answer. In March 2025, President Trump told Congress that China's commercial and naval shipbuilding capacity is more than 230 times ours, and his April executive order, "Restoring America's Maritime Dominance," states plainly that America builds less than one percent of the world's commercial ships while China builds about half. So how did the renaissance's first full year go? By one industry count, America built five commercial ships. China built about a thousand. China took 75 percent of the world's new orders; Korea took 19; the United States took 0.2 percent. Of the fifteen cargo ships on American order books, twelve will be mostly constructed -- in Korea. Of our 66 shipyards, eight can fully build new ships from scratch. That is the gap Port Alpha is meant to close, one drone boat at a time.
None of this is an argument against the yard. Ten thousand jobs in the Rio Grande Valley are real, and a country that cannot float its own tonnage has problems no tariff can fix. It's an argument against grading a renaissance on ceremony. 2024 was a high-water mark -- pull-forward buying, Red Sea diversions -- so going flat under it means falling behind a world that kept growing. A shipyard is a thirty-year bet on cargo that hasn't come back.
Ships follow cargo. Cargo follows prosperity. And prosperity, by the dock receipts, is the one thing that hasn't moved since 2024. You can break a lot of ground in Brownsville. You cannot break the tide with a ceremony. The renaissance will arrive the day the water says so -- measured in TEUs, not photo ops. The first phase of Port Alpha opens in 2028. Check the water.

Source notes & caveats - Ceremony (Sept. 30, 2026): Austin American-Statesman, gCaptain, Texas Governor's office, Saronic release. The 10,000 jobs and $264.5B are Saronic/state projections, not delivered outcomes. Vance's exact phrase: "the American dream renewed."
\- Volume: NRF/Hackett Global Port Tracker -- 2024 ≈ 25.5M TEU; 2025 = 25.4M; 2026 forecast ≈ 25.7M (+1%), H1 2026 +1.1%. Descartes monthly reports give the shocks (May 2025 −11.4% m/m; Sept 2025 −8.4% m/m, China −22.9% y/y; Nov 2025 China −12.5% m/m). Trackers differ modestly (Descartes' all-ports figure also has 2025 at −0.4% vs 2024) -- the plateau holds either way.
\- Honest framing of "decline": 2024 was a near-record base (front-loading, Red Sea diversions), so the accurate story is a three-year flat line beneath a high-water mark plus violent monthly swings -- not a straight-line collapse. The essay says exactly that, so it can't be charged with cherry-picking.
\- Value data: USTR -- 2025 goods imports from China $308.7B, −29.9%; deficit $202.7B, −31.8%. Trump's 230x figure comes from the March 4, 2025 address (USNI reported "232 times"); the "<1% of commercial ships / China ~half" line is from the April 9, 2025 EO itself. "Five ships built in 2025" is BRS Shipbrokers' count via the New York Post; federal tallies vary by category.

The monthly ledger is where the politics shows. May 2025, the tariff shock: imports fell 11.4 percent in a single month, China down 20.8. September 2025 brought the steepest monthly drop in years -- down 8.4 percent, with China-origin volume down 22.9 percent year over year and China's share of U.S. imports sliding from 34.5 to 33 percent in one month. October fell 7.5 percent below the year before. January 2026 came in 6.4 percent under January 2025, and the first quarter was forecast down 9 to 17 percent. June 2026 surged 14.3 percent -- but only because June 2025 had been gutted. Ocean contract rates fell last year for the first time since July 2024. Hackett Associates, whose data underlies NRF's tracker, said it plainly: a small decline for 2025 versus 2024, "and a further, larger decline in the first quarter of 2026." The tide didn't collapse in one wave. It stopped rising. And if the goal was independence from Chinese trade, the value numbers say the tariffs did what they promised: U.S. goods imports from China fell 29.9 percent in 2025 -- $131.7 billion gone in a single year -- and the bilateral deficit dropped 31.8 percent. But here's what nobody put on the podium: total import volume did not grow to replace it. It went nowhere. We didn't trade China for Texas. We traded volume for slogans. This matters because of what the ceremony claimed to answer. In March 2025, President Trump told Congress that China's commercial and naval shipbuilding capacity is more than 230 times ours, and his April executive order, "Restoring America's Maritime Dominance," states plainly that America builds less than one percent of the world's commercial ships while China builds about half. So how did the renaissance's first full year go? By one industry count, America built five commercial ships. China built about a thousand. China took 75 percent of the world's new orders; Korea took 19; the United States took 0.2 percent. Of the fifteen cargo ships on American order books, twelve will be mostly constructed -- in Korea. Of our 66 shipyards, eight can fully build new ships from scratch. That is the gap Port Alpha is meant to close, one drone boat at a time. None of this is an argument against the yard. Ten thousand jobs in the Rio Grande Valley are real, and a country that cannot float its own tonnage has problems no tariff can fix. It's an argument against grading a renaissance on ceremony. 2024 was a high-water mark -- pull-forward buying, Red Sea diversions -- so going flat under it means falling behind a world that kept growing. A shipyard is a thirty-year bet on cargo that hasn't come back. Ships follow cargo. Cargo follows prosperity. And prosperity, by the dock receipts, is the one thing that hasn't moved since 2024. You can break a lot of ground in Brownsville. You cannot break the tide with a ceremony. The renaissance will arrive the day the water says so -- measured in TEUs, not photo ops. The first phase of Port Alpha opens in 2028. Check the water. Source notes & caveats - Ceremony (Sept. 30, 2026): Austin American-Statesman, gCaptain, Texas Governor's office, Saronic release. The 10,000 jobs and $264.5B are Saronic/state projections, not delivered outcomes. Vance's exact phrase: "the American dream renewed." \- Volume: NRF/Hackett Global Port Tracker -- 2024 ≈ 25.5M TEU; 2025 = 25.4M; 2026 forecast ≈ 25.7M (+1%), H1 2026 +1.1%. Descartes monthly reports give the shocks (May 2025 −11.4% m/m; Sept 2025 −8.4% m/m, China −22.9% y/y; Nov 2025 China −12.5% m/m). Trackers differ modestly (Descartes' all-ports figure also has 2025 at −0.4% vs 2024) -- the plateau holds either way. \- Honest framing of "decline": 2024 was a near-record base (front-loading, Red Sea diversions), so the accurate story is a three-year flat line beneath a high-water mark plus violent monthly swings -- not a straight-line collapse. The essay says exactly that, so it can't be charged with cherry-picking. \- Value data: USTR -- 2025 goods imports from China $308.7B, −29.9%; deficit $202.7B, −31.8%. Trump's 230x figure comes from the March 4, 2025 address (USNI reported "232 times"); the "<1% of commercial ships / China ~half" line is from the April 9, 2025 EO itself. "Five ships built in 2025" is BRS Shipbrokers' count via the New York Post; federal tallies vary by category. You're currently a free subscriber to . | | Hello, Friend, I hope you're doing well today. I'm reaching out to share something that's been on my mind lately...

Are you as concerned about the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) as I am? Many Americans are--and for good reason.

While AI-powered chatbots and search engines can be quite helpful, artificial intelligence can also be used in harmful and even deadly ways.

For example, in the war between Russia and Ukraine, both countries are utilizing AI in an effort to make their drones and other weapons more and more deadly.

And in China, the ruling Communist Party uses AI to control its population, which enables China to punish dissidents and reward loyalists more effectively.

**In other words, AI, like every other technology, can be used for good or for ill. **

As American citizens, our task is to ensure that AI technology is used to preserve rather than to destroy freedom.

That's why Hillsdale College created a free online video series to help you understand what AI means for our future--and our freedom.

This fascinating, FREE online video series examines artificial intelligence, including its relationship to human nature, the threat it poses to self-government, and its uses on the battlefield.

**STATE-BY-STATE OUTLOOK**
**IDAHO — PROPOSITION 1 — VOTE YES ✅**
Proposition 1 would establish a statutory right to reproductive freedom and privacy, including abortion before fetal viability and in medical emergencies, as well as decisions involving contraception, fertility treatment, miscarriage care, childbirth, and prenatal and postpartum care. A YES vote would enact those protections.
**MISSOURI — AMENDMENT 3 — VOTE NO ❌**
Missouri voters approved constitutional reproductive-health-care protections in 2024, including abortion through fetal viability. Amendment 3 would repeal those protections and replace them with substantially narrower provisions allowing abortion in specified circumstances. A NO vote would leave the 2024 reproductive-health-care protections in place.
**NEVADA — QUESTION 6 — VOTE YES ✅**
Question 6 would add abortion protections to the Nevada Constitution. Nevada voters approved the amendment once in 2024; because it is a citizen-initiated constitutional amendment, voters must approve it again in 2026 for it to take effect.
**VIRGINIA — QUESTION 1 — VOTE YES ✅**
Question 1 would add constitutional protections for reproductive decisions including abortion, contraception, fertility care, miscarriage management, prenatal care, childbirth, and postpartum care.
**THE BOTTOM LINE** These fights won't be easy. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi, I know you get a lot of emails from me. So I wanted to
take a step back and tell you a little bit more about me and why I’m
running to be the next Governor of Michigan.

Ever since I was a student, I knew I wanted to fight for justice and make
a difference. I’m the daughter of two special education teachers. I was
raised in a working class family that instilled in me the values of hard
work, opportunity, and serving others.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights in the US and abroad.

It’s why I became a law clerk in Detroit, fighting to protect and defend
people’s civil rights and freedoms.

It’s why, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to ensure
all students could afford their education, froze tuition, and expanded
scholarships.

And it’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life
easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter
access.

But I know our work is far from finished. So now, I’m running for Governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone – from our kids to our
seniors – can stay and thrive.

I know that government works best when it’s there when you need it, and
gets out of the way when you don’t. So here’s my promise to you: when we
win this election, I will use every tool available to make life easier:
expand rural healthcare options, build more housing, take on the utility
companies who raise our rates, make childcare free, and ensure anyone can
afford to live in the best place to call home.

But here’s the truth: Michigan is one of the most competitive states in
the entire country, and my opponent has the backing of big billionaires
and special interests. I can only win this race with your support, so
today, I’m asking:

name: Fred Clark
subject: Open for pie crust
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Clark for Wisconsin Clark for Wisconsin
body:
| | |
---
---
Peter, Running for office is go, go, go. Most days are some mix of driving across the district, speaking with voters at events, and eating whatever I can grab between stops. But I'm glad I can still make time for the things I love. And I still enjoy making a real fruit pie. A pie crust is one of the things I'm proudest of in the kitchen. The recipe I use is from _Joy of Cooking_ , and it’s one my mother and grandmother both used, and the secret is ice water with vinegar. The ingredients for an all butter pie crust are simple, but it's the technique that makes the difference! You may need to practice this a few times, but you'll know you got it right when that crust just shatters when you bite it. Once you get the hang of it, you’ll be making this pie crust for all your events, with any fruit that's in season.

**I want to share the recipe for this incredible pie crust, and I hope you'll try it soon, to celebrate the beginning of fall. If you do, send me a photo. I'd love to see how it turns out.**
---
|
---
**Joy of Cooking Classic All Butter Pie Crust **_The classic all-butter pie or pastry dough recipe from the Joy of Cooking yields one 9- or 10-inch double crust (or two single crusts)._

**Ingredients**
**All-purpose flour:** 21⁄2 cups (315g)
**Sugar:** 1 tsp (optional)
**Salt:** 1⁄2 tsp
**Cold unsalted butter:** 2 sticks (225g), cubed and kept very cold
**Ice water with vinegar:** 6 tablespoons of ice water mixed with 1 tablespoon of distilled white or cider vinegar
**Extra ice water:** 1 to 3 teaspoons, if the dough is too dry

**Instructions**
1\. **Mix dry ingredients:** Whisk or pulse the flour, sugar, and salt together in a large bowl.
2\. **Cut in the butter:** Add the cold, cubed butter and cut it into the flour using a pastry blender, two knives, or your fingers until the pieces are pea-sized or resemble coarse crumbs, leaving some visible bits of butter.
3.**Add liquid:** Drizzle the ice water and vinegar mixture over the flour and butter. Gently blend or stir with a spatula or fork just until the dough holds together when squeezed. Add extra drops of ice water if parts remain too dry.
4\. **Shape and chill:** Divide the dough in half. Shape each half into a flat disk, wrap tightly, and chill in the refrigerator for 30 to 60 minutes before rolling out.

Happy baking,
Fred

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/80890684-97b7-4f70-96ea-385e82d1f97d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Interest rates are on an upward march. The 10-year Treasury just hit 5.33%; the 30-year hit 5.69%. Those are 24-year highs. But this is not just an American phenomenon. The UK 30-year punched through 6% for the first time since 1998. France's 10-year hit its highest since 2002. The bond market is telegraphing distress.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ded5f31d-dcb7-4eaf-bec7-da2270eb8358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What is going on? The answer comes down to three forces. And they're all connected.
**1\. Inflation: Stimulus & War**
The inflation story started with COVID. Governments flooded their economies with trillions in stimulus, central banks monetized it, and demand came roaring back before supply chains could. That was the first wave. The second wave came from two wars. Russia's invasion of Ukraine rapidly and massively disrupted the energy and grain markets, beginning in 2022 but continuing to the present. The Iran war compounded an already problematic situation: Goldman Sachs called the Iran War the largest oil supply shock in history. Brent hit $126. Diesel is at $6.43 a gallon. The correlation between oil prices and the 10-year yield is now 0.96--nearly perfect, according to BMO Capital Markets.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/83198b0e-1007-4ece-967e-9a46b96742b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I've written for months about the Iran War's ripple effects--from the Strait of Hormuz and global food security to the cost of everything that moves by truck. This was never a war contained to the Middle East. It crossed the oceans through the gas pump, the grocery store, and now mortgage rates (recently north of 7%). Layer on tariffs, reshoring of supply chains, and a world bifurcating into Chinese-led and US-led economic blocs, and you get higher costs.
**2\. Artificial Intelligence: Competing and Concealing**
Five companies have issued over $400 billion in bonds to build data centers. That's $400 billion of investor cash that didn't go into Treasuries. One analyst told CNBC the AI buildout is now a bigger driver of yields than inflation: "I think this year it has more to do with the bond issuance than the inflation story."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9269694e-3863-4897-9db6-cc9836c0f7c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But there's a paradox in the AI infrastructure boom. AI capex is also the only thing making GDP growth look resilient. I've argued the U.S. economy might just be three data centers in a trench coat: strip out AI spending and growth is essentially zero. But the Fed looks at headline GDP, sees "strength," and keeps rates high.
* * *
## [AI Infrastructure: Boom or Bust?](https://substack.com/redirect/1fc6656a-5bb2-47b1-8f6b-cc01c6e21fa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[In the late 1990s, Lucent Technologies was America's most widely held stock -- a "picks and shovels" play on the internet revolution. The company lent billions to its own customers so they could buy more Lucent equipment. On paper, revenue soared. In reality, Lucent was financing its own demand. When the customers went bust, Lucent nearly followed. The p...](https://substack.com/redirect/1fc6656a-5bb2-47b1-8f6b-cc01c6e21fa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
So the same buildout that's masking a recession is also crowding the bond market and blocking the rate relief the rest of the economy needs. This "trench coat economy" has a price, and the bond market is charging it.
**3\. Deficits & Debt **
US debt is now more than $40 trillion. The US defense budget crossed $1 trillion for the first time due in large part to the ongoing war in the Middle East. Politicians have no will to cut, and the baby bust makes the math worse: 18 consecutive years of falling US births means a shrinking tax base servicing a growing debt. And lest we think the deficit and debt problem is just an American issue, think again. OECD governments are borrowing $18 trillion this year.
The supply of bonds is exploding. Demand is thinning. Chinese surpluses that used to recycle into Treasuries are no longer heading to Washington. Japan sold a record $87.8 billion of foreign bonds in a single month to defend the yen. Domestic financial stress is forcing the repatriation of capital. The incremental buyer (and holder?) of government debt has gone from price-insensitive central banks to price-sensitive hedge funds and investment managers who demand to be paid for bearing risk.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1017cf76-feb7-445f-b19b-21fbb8eff99a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When a country's deficits are (or need to be) financed by foreigners who are no longer buying, the country has a choice: either pay up in yield or lets the currency depreciate. Japan is choosing yield defense. In America, similar dynamics are less severe due to the US dollars role as the global reserve currency. But persistent deficits and vanishing foreign buyers is a world where the exorbitant privilege the dollar affords the United States gets renegotiated, slowly and then, quite possibly. suddenly.
**What higher rates mean**
Rising rates don't just slow an economy. They expose weaknesses.
Start with affordability. Mortgages above 7% have frozen the housing market; sellers won't give up 3% loans and buyers can't qualify at 7%. Credit card and auto rates are at generational highs. Add >$6 diesel and higher grocery prices, and the household budget is squeezed from both sides.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/429db591-d89a-453d-a739-55abcf5cc00d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That squeeze is intensifying an already-problematic K-shaped economy. Asset owners (meaning those with paid-off homes, stock portfolios, and cash) are fine. Everyone else is not. Consumer confidence is plunging. Real estate is deteriorating. Unemployment is drifting up, and AI is part of why: the same capex that props up GDP and makes the economy appear resilient is, upon deeper scrutiny, automating white-collar work and hollowing out hiring.
Under the surface is an economy that desperately needs lower rates and can't get them, because the trench coat makes it look like lower rates are not justified.
**The wage-price spiral worry**
Central bankers regularly fret about runaway inflation, the kind incited by a wage-price spiral: workers see prices rise, demand higher wages, firms raise prices to cover the wages, and the cycle feeds itself. That's what entrenched inflation in the 1970s, and it's a legitimate thing to watch.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fc493aae-c6cc-4863-8da3-4608581a50bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But it should be a secondary concern. A wage-price spiral requires workers with bargaining power, and bargaining power requires a tight labor market. It's hard to demand a raise when you don't have a job. With unemployment rising, AI displacing roles, and consumer confidence collapsing, the greater risk isn't that wages chase prices. It's that central bankers are fighting the last war while the current one (a very weak economy wearing a strong economy's clothes) goes unaddressed.
**Three dots, one trend**
Covid- and war-driven inflation. An AI boom that masks weakness while competing for capital. Growing deficits, rising debt issuance, and fewer and fewer buyers of that debt. All three dots point to an increasingly fragile economy that's precariously teetering on the AI investment story. Time for caution.

When I made the decision to run against Greg Abbott, I knew I was facing an uphill battle.
In January, one of the first public polls of this race had us down eight points. Abbott has been governor for more than a decade. He has a massive campaign war chest, billionaire donors ready to spend whatever it takes to keep him in power, and every advantage an incumbent could ask for.
**But Texans had something else in mind.**
Month by month, we closed the gap.
In May, polling showed us five points behind. By July, we were within a single point. Then came polls showing us three points behind, one point behind, and **TIED at 47 -47**. Now, a new poll from the _New York Times_ has us leading against Greg Abbott -- _the third poll showing us up in the last three weeks._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/33683ffb-266a-43cd-b0c9-5f0d9e0abd7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Even The Cook Political Report just shifted this race in our favor for the _second_ time since August.
**With just weeks until Election Day, one thing is clear: This race is competitive, and Texans have a real choice about the future of our state.**
That didn't happen overnight.
We went across Texas -- from Brownsville to Amarillo and El Paso to DFW -- talking to the people who have spent years feeling like they are getting the short end of the stick.
We talked to parents worried about the future of their neighborhood schools. We talked to families watching their electricity, grocery, housing, and healthcare costs skyrocket. We talked to communities being forced to sacrifice their land and water for massive data centers while billionaire corporations get special treatment.
And everywhere I go, I hear some version of the same thing: **Texans are tired of paying more and getting less.**
For more than a decade, Greg Abbott has had the opportunity to make life better for working families. Instead, Texans have watched him prioritize special interest groups and his ultra-wealthy donors all while everyday families struggle to get ahead.
That's what I call the _Greg Abbott Corruption Tax_ -- when the people with the most money and influence get to skip the line while the rest of us foot the bill. When I'm governor, that ends.
**I 'm running to secure the American Dream in Texas by saving our neighborhood schools, putting a moratorium on data center construction and putting money back in your pocket.** Every Texan deserves to have a seat at the table.
A lot can and will happen in this race between now and Election Day. What matters is what we do with the opportunity in front of us.
We have changed the trajectory of this race. **But we haven 't won anything yet.**
There are still millions of Texans we need to reach. We're still knocking on doors, funding ads, and recruiting volunteers to help make sure that we win on Election Day.
We have spent nearly a year proving that change is possible. Now we have just a few weeks to make it happen.
**[So I'm humbly asking you to help us finish what we started. If you believe Texas deserves new leadership, will you please chip in $5, $10, or whatever makes sense for you today to help us reach as many voters as possible in these final weeks?](https://substack.com/redirect/83df8095-74a3-4b09-aba5-0534236935ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/33683ffb-266a-43cd-b0c9-5f0d9e0abd7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We didn't come this far just to come this close.
Let's win this -- together.
-- Gina

Friends,
If you've been reading my Substack posts with any regularity, you know I've spent the last few months crisscrossing Kansas, listening to thousands of people. What you might _not_ realize is that no matter where I go, people ask me one question over and over again.
Folks will say to me, "I can't figure you out. Are you liberal or conservative?"
My answer, every time, is: "Yes, of course."
They look at me for a second, and then most of the time, they say, "No, no, _which are you?_ "
I understand why they're asking. In these deeply divided times, people put a lot of stock in how we label ourselves politically. If someone identifies as a liberal, people think they know what that person stands for. Same if someone defines themselves as a conservative. But like I tell the people who ask me which I am:_**I think we can -- and must -- be both.**_
Let me explain.
**To be liberal can mean to be generous of spirit, open to reform and to seeing things with fresh eyes. To be conservative can mean holding onto values and beliefs that are really important.**
Those are both important perspectives to bring to the table -- and I think at some level, we all know we are not 100% one or the other all of the time. Maybe you think of yourself as an incredibly liberal person. I bet you're still conservative compared to _someone_ you know. And if you identify as deeply conservative -- well, I bet you can still think of someone that _you 're _liberal compared to.
That's why I don't focus on the political label. I think what matters far more is whether you stand up for your neighbors and your community. And after talking to thousands of people throughout the state, I think Kansans agree with me. That's probably why I've had more people than I can count come up to me and say, "I've never voted for a Democrat, but I'm going to vote for you."
**Friends, despite what the media and career politicians would have us believe, the division and polarization that have taken root in this country aren 't serving any of us. We need each other -- we really do. We're better together. Our systems only function when we work with each other ... when we fight a bit and argue some, then come up with a compromise that takes into account the concerns of both sides.**
Maybe I can see this more clearly because I'm _not_ a career politician. I've said all along that my focus is on serving **everyone**. I've shared that unifying message everywhere I've visited, and people have responded because, in their hearts, I think they realize we're better off together, too -- regardless of whether someone calls themselves a liberal or a conservative.
Liberal or conservative, what really matters is how we show up for people. Whether we're generous of spirit, see things with new eyes and are open to making things better -- while at the same time holding onto the values and beliefs that define us. _In other words, it 's about being liberal **and** conservative, and finding ways to connect with the people around us, no matter what they choose to call themselves. That's been the foundation of my campaign, and if I'm elected, it will keep being my focus while I'm in Washington._
**In the final stretch of this race, it 's more important than ever to make sure every voter understands that I will fight for them, regardless of their political affiliation. But time is getting short. With early voting starting in Kansas in less than two weeks, we need to keep our momentum going.**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/bbf840f5-594b-4d1b-ab61-6b6e99ae4509?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for all you do,
Adam Hamilton

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/375b7191-108d-4cee-9e69-3ca274956352?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**by[Lawrence Winnerman](https://substack.com/redirect/629d9dc8-5e5e-41b0-b351-d79dc45e21d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
A couple of months ago, I wrote an article called "[The Layer War](https://substack.com/redirect/a444c9d0-0b8c-4a3c-aecd-65bcf56ecd85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," where I postulated that big tech and the AI Frontier Labs were splitting into two camps: the Builders and the Layerers. The Builders were the ones who were spending hundreds of billions of dollars constructing actual physical infrastructure of AI: the data centers and the servers, and, in some cases, even the electrical generation needed to power the servers in those data centers.
The Layerers were the ones who were betting that AI becomes a cheap commodity, and the money will settle into the software layering on top of whatever intelligence you want to use. The thing is, right now it sort of looks like the Builders might be right, and they're building to win. They are willing to dump as much money is needed to build out the physical infrastructure for their models. And they're no longer paying in cash--they're borrowing.
The scale of the amount of money that they're borrowing is hard to conceptualize. Morgan Stanley said it expects the six largest hyperscalers to spend $785 billion on capital projects this year and close to $1 trillion next year, with more than $1.2 trillion in data center leases already committed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4ed91ee8-3c60-4892-9e5c-ad5c3a33681b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas expects $3 trillion to $5 trillion of buildout over the next 3 to 5 years, and of that, it thinks about $300 billion of it is going to be AI-related investment-grade bonds this year alone. Investment-grade AI-related bonds are competition for investment against the Fed's own Treasury notes.
In essence, the builders' AI data center buildouts are so incomprehensibly expensive that they require incredible amounts of borrowing, some of which will be funded through sales of their own bonds and others of which are completely agnostic about the current interest rate.
What does that mean? It means that the frontier labs building the data centers don't care what the interest rate is. They can't afford to care about the interest rate. They are price takers. They will take whatever price is offered to them.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=218826550&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4ODI2NTUwLCJpYXQiOjE3OTExNDQ2NDAsImV4cCI6MTc5MzczNjY0MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ya7ukGm6NmRi0PvOmikcQQNe98t82Dx7JWnHOC4Mfxk&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
## Can you take any price offered? Of course not.
Imagine if this were true of people. I live in northeast Indiana--a red corner of a very red state. This is the kind of place where a $250,000 home is still a reality. The kind of place with three bedrooms and a garage, and a furnace, where you could happily raise a family, if you didn't mind the local politics.
This is the kind of place where people pay attention to the interest rate because it affects everything from credit cards, personal loans, car loans, boat loans, and, of course, mortgages.
Last week, the 10-year Treasury note closed the week near 5.28%. That's just a few basis points below the 24-year high it set on Wednesday. The 30-year note sits at about 5.61%. Oil spent the week at or above $100 a barrel. And to top everything off all of that rolled up to lending rates across the board. Freddie Mac reported that the average 30-year mortgage had jumped a quarter point in a single week to 7.28%.
If you take out a mortgage on that $250,000 home, you probably put down about 10%, and so your 30-year loan is for $225,000. In the last several months, the interest rate for that loan rose from 6.34% to 7.28%, which is $140 more a month for your payment, or more than $50,000 over the life of the load. For many people, that's a decision not to buy the house.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=218826550&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE4ODI2NTUwLCJpYXQiOjE3OTExNDQ2NDAsImV4cCI6MTc5MzczNjY0MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ya7ukGm6NmRi0PvOmikcQQNe98t82Dx7JWnHOC4Mfxk)
Here's a thing that sounds disconnected, but it isn't. The week before, CNBC ran a story about what rising yields mean for the AI Frontier Labs. A strategist named Mark Malak of Seabert Financial said something that I haven't been able to stop thinking about. According to him, the AI builders are "basically price insensitive to that raise, which means they're price takers."
This is where that phrase "price takers" comes in. When it comes to financial markets, a "price taker" isn't the kind of thing you want to be. It means that you don't have any other choice, so you take the price that's offered, even when somebody else walks away. It's a strange thing to call the richest companies on Earth, and it's also a thread that runs through all those numbers above.
Which is the point. Walking away is what higher interest rates are for. It's what they're supposed to make people do.
## How the brakes are supposed to work
For better or for worse, when the Fed raises interest rates because of inflation, what it's trying to do is put the brakes on the economy.

name: Ryan Grim
subject: Survivors of One of America's Worst War Crimes Since Vietnam Speak
body:
Once in a while, though too often for comfort, there are events that remind us why we do the work we do.

| |
---|---|---
|
# Survivors of One of America's Worst War Crimes Since Vietnam Speak
| | | [Ryan Grim](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
| Oct 4
---
| [](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
Once in a while, though too often for comfort, there are events that remind us why we do the work we do. One of those came on February 28, 2026, when the U.S. launched its joint war with Israel against Iran with an attack on a school building in Minab while hundreds of children were beginning their day.
My colleagues Jeremy Scahill and Murtaza Hussain and journalist Reza Sayah spent the last two months exploring the depths of that atrocity, speaking to survivors, parents, first responders, government officials, and medical personnel who had the inconceivable task of treating the wounded while grieving their own children killed in the attack--or uncertain of their fate.
In the U.S., after a school shooting, news outlets excel at painting portraits of those whose lives were horrifically cut short. When it comes to the children murdered in Minab, there has been no such dignity afforded to them. We hope in some small way to offer some.
Jeremy's article is a hard read, but an important one, and you'll be glad you took the time with it. **[Read it here.](https://substack.com/redirect/b6b86ca4-a977-4100-bfca-56a8d5d9b61e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** And please share it with anyone in your life who needs the reminder of what we are capable of. We also produced a video that gives a visceral sense of the sheer depravity of the attack, and the way that it has fundamentally changed a community forever. **[Watch it on YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/9593aca5-3b81-4444-8165-7439779e7848?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or Substack, below.**
Thank you for reading, for watching, and for being part of a community of readers unafraid of the truth.

body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Patriot,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. # **OFFICIAL MEMORANDUM**
****
__From the Desk of Donald J. Trump__ ____
There is a price for threatening the system. I have paid it.
[](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
The courtrooms. The investigations. Two impeachments. A mugshot they plastered across the world, hoping to humiliate a president who would not kneel. And in Butler, Pennsylvania, a bullet that came within an inch of ending it all. I got back up. I raised my fist. I kept fighting.
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
Most presidents never pay that price, because most presidents never threaten the people who actually run Washington. They sign what they are told to sign. They look the other way. They leave with their reputation intact and the country worse than they found it. The system never hits them, because they were never a threat.
I was. From the first day I went after the open border, the factories they shipped overseas, and the corruption they thought nobody would touch. They noticed. They came after me with everything they had. I carried it so you would not have to.
**_I cannot carry it alone forever._** **__**
Tonight I am asking for your eyes and your prayers.
[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
We are less than 4 weeks out from the midterms. The left wants the final nail. If they take the House, the border reopens, your taxes go up, and everything we fought for is on the table. You have watched me take the hits. You have watched me get back up. Sitting this one out is not standing with me.
**_[I have never asked for sympathy. I am asking you to pray, and then to go on the record, right now, before this gets away from us.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)_**

[STAND WITH TRUMP](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)

body:
Every call we make will move these races forward and impact the national balance of power.
#
Hi there,
Flipping the House will come down to a handful of congressional districts around the country. If you’re looking for a high-impact way to support Democrats running in some of the most competitive House races this year, there’s a very special volunteer opportunity coming up next week!
**On October 14th at 8 PM ET, Lin-Manuel Miranda and special guests will be hosting a virtual phone bank in support of five House candidates who make up the Miranda Family Rising Stars Fund!**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2430?utm_source=em20261004-3024&t=1&akid=3024%2E1562180%2EIki9Nw)
This year, the Miranda Family Rising Stars Fund is supporting Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Joanna Mendoza (AZ-06), Denise Powell (NE-02), Manny Rutinel (CO-08), and Randy Villegas (CA-22)—five Latino candidates running in some of the country's most competitive races.
We’ll kick off the night live with Lin-Manuel Miranda and other special guests, then each volunteer will be matched with a Rising Star candidate and call voters directly in their district.
**All scripts, training, and dialers are provided. No experience is necessary—just bring positive energy and a phone and computer!**
[**Space is limited, so make sure to RSVP here to reserve your spot in the (virtual) room where it happens.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2430?utm_source=em20261004-3024&t=2&akid=3024%2E1562180%2EIki9Nw)
Every call we make will move these races forward and impact the national balance of power. This is a rare chance to campaign directly alongside Lin-Manuel Miranda for candidates who will define the next Congress, and we hope to see you there!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261004-3&t=3&refcode2=3024_1562180_Iki9Nw&akid=3024%2E1562180%2EIki9Nw)

Patriot,
_**For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience.** _ She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. **For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her.** **For 45 days, she suffered a living hell.** **For 45 days, she endured untold horrors.** [ _**Then came Day 46. That was the day our team at Heroes for Humanity went in and brought her out.** _ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=af0cb050d9c64a82be960d030c36319f&_e=kAs4FmRTEs05RiDVKg3T1ix0Mfw6WDLRDGfNs2fesiURD1f-N-hU1B3tQN4SK-gIvP1bK-fgHOOcxYqgA7eprEDSK0q5MQ8oH3fkzuCe07prNHqJ2ebbcWSxkJlEI-_QtTErAlXwqtZDW9_VDTrvIxptNuF4rkdyRvOGyItpYmEIf9jrVEFJ6xenlHlRM110aLgyd9lgCPSszhODi8bmFlz6iGiYgaGhjtKEnh1i2O8-LcohgqT4SmiUb0KrvUkU-0XVisN2JKXzirwpb_qh-CSWNmXXOFqbbpBrR2yFr7e8nOSnEBggYoFZ61hY5H61jNuHxtCRxy6lhefCqYyeM56_cZyd0GVG7F7W2so9-KVj4q2ipJwiv8x-pWkxmRryRbvOc7SpncxpDLf0_nc3lODBlNcPT_dAJ9zBik58t0h9pyKBj8CBWrGlgBORYkyeZ0hctb2G5rtBeheqEzPszskppWPQEG9IGgj1G1P2NsFA-Vt9r0CSLpzD0r_p6qRK)
My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. **That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way.** We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. [ _**For that little girl, it meant getting her out of an unimaginable situation and bringing her home.** _ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=af0cb050d9c64a82be960d030c36319f&_e=kAs4FmRTEs05RiDVKg3T1ix0Mfw6WDLRDGfNs2fesiURD1f-N-hU1B3tQN4SK-gIvP1bK-fgHOOcxYqgA7eprEDSK0q5MQ8oH3fkzuCe07prNHqJ2ebbcWSxkJlEI-_QtTErAlXwqtZDW9_VDTrvI3gBkF0JGMWpHhWW9AlZb9bAtNMiF1WBp0z_2UCHz9CfND19wSUYcL7Fh3JrOXpRpudbIu3jnA5jYDUEmGlwh1hprxEAGxjM2hfMOxCJtXCPk54QPafMBA8kD7ZFjO6bPlpdJqXj2d1CT0EpS6pOK7f1OtIhgnDku5fKyps4FjavSa5PA3EWEvdNmlg4qJBtRATSyq2Rcw1raPb0jeindUYkuPi2T7QMMPuu0WMT3s-j8Oy_RbEC3ILKwbJe2VDP22Irwd9S81OmbjPOJgxaVkjhulxbO-R0_0aMQvyUWeIjWcaAxi-pMn-mW2O-aPyhngj-eaSdycNuGiDIeXFXoQZg7rYTmTwOX1p5m-m3z961) In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. But we can't wait until the next desperate call comes to get ready. Our operators have to be trained. Our equipment has to be ready. Vehicles need fuel. Medical supplies need to be stocked. Because when someone is waiting for their “Day 46,” every minute matters. **So, I’m asking you to do something today.** [ _**Will you make a gift of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to Heroes for Humanity?** _ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=af0cb050d9c64a82be960d030c36319f&_e=kAs4FmRTEs05RiDVKg3T1ix0Mfw6WDLRDGfNs2fesiURD1f-N-hU1B3tQN4SK-gIvP1bK-fgHOOcxYqgA7eprEDSK0q5MQ8oH3fkzuCe07prNHqJ2ebbcWSxkJlEI-_QtTErAlXwqtZDW9_VDTrvIyjZN0OWyvq92kPpkextChBiZVO3bAfAZ7BJ_b2O18WMftd0mGKOnT4hrkHdqABBqZKBknqDonZuSbHJJvJueR2bvN_zjj4wBxtWwqzpO9C_lWJZ_D5vecwIet12eRNGQmqU3MiMTOsvE5-bqB9AeUKmCwX4Ye1M6BDUbnH1JFZV4_yP6HmCN2lbxNU4wyeA2oyKqBnR5wI4lLfv-rHRI5eeZnYzCIpbwI_BRH46SWXUmP8KsA9JjmfR_7J_BVH1HeDvCeQZr-6kwBjUx5QDYxQ_Dg6NMbpaLBccGVb2romy0tmmAXQCTXVXnHjdDx5aZCaqBns-1DZPj4YEdefSGsQdGTtRDLyTAHLhhLbIVWaH) You may never be the person who physically walks into danger to bring someone home, but you can empower someone else to be that person. Your gift can be the hand that reaches across the world to comfort someone in need. [ _**And maybe, just maybe, God put this message in front of you today for a reason.** _ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=af0cb050d9c64a82be960d030c36319f&_e=kAs4FmRTEs05RiDVKg3T1ix0Mfw6WDLRDGfNs2fesiURD1f-N-hU1B3tQN4SK-gIvP1bK-fgHOOcxYqgA7eprEDSK0q5MQ8oH3fkzuCe07prNHqJ2ebbcWSxkJlEI-_QtTErAlXwqtZDW9_VDTrvIy1oYM8GSiTqGfPMIOX7kqS3GSRk8XJITS_u05YI_Ud8MiNkj1b27UJGrZaj6oGF_xOYQCpeRlLRbn9OWrwy6kUBzCaCXaPwmpqNDgu9bZJYHYp9aVBXM8vNfuxU94NoVsN2K2nHIzgTKdjZsJMXdGSyk4zLVOI-eUDJDAaLtO_1d1NmzZYGv7d1qwfFKwK2pu_lP6H6JyhwWflDNcyjAln5YCaLECU9HnP5YnhwfXnVITYgArj5G9yJsHuW1fN9w_mHwSH5rPZlMk-ccAOj4m4C70v7Kx-5cpcWGMHgYR4pYqS52lec27ZVB0k4rtGQAoQipD8zNyQydy6o3306lO3FeGUVqYO-Z2zhJsKlEH3c)

clean_body: For 45 days, she was alone and abandoned. For 45 days, she was alone and abandoned. | | | | | Patriot, For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience. She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her. For 45 days, she suffered a living hell. For 45 days, she endured untold horrors. My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way. We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. But we can't wait until the next desperate call comes to get ready. Our operators have to be trained. Our equipment has to be ready. Vehicles need fuel. Medical supplies need to be stocked. Because when someone is waiting for their “Day 46,” every minute matters. So, I’m asking you to do something today. You may never be the person who physically walks into danger to bring someone home, but you can empower someone else to be that person. Your gift can be the hand that reaches across the world to comfort someone in need. | "HELP ANSWER THE NEXT CALL" There will always be another person who needs someone to come for them. With your help, when that call comes, we'll be ready to echo the Biblical prophets and say, “Here am I. Send me.” Respectfully submitted, Dennis Price CEO & Founder Heroes for Humanity | | | | | | | | SERVING THE VULNERABLE. SHARING THE GOSPEL. Tesla Is Pulling Car Lines Out of Fremont to Build Robots. Follow the Part Inside Every One.
Fremont is being retooled for a million humanoid robots a year. Musk warns the ramp will be slow and hard. That’s exactly why the scarce components every robot needs could be the quieter, steadier way to play the boom.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Car factories built the 20th century’s fortunes. Tesla is now pulling car production lines out of its Fremont plant to build something else: humanoid robots. The headlines will go to the robots. History says the steadier money often goes somewhere quieter: the parts every robot needs, no matter who builds it.
The evidence board
| | What’s Actually Happening
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the factory.** Tesla is phasing out its Model S and Model X lines at Fremont to make room for Optimus production, with a first-generation line designed for about 1 million robots a year. A second facility at Giga Texas targets up to 10 million a year over the long term.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the warning.** Musk himself says Optimus “is going to be the hardest to scale in manufacturing that we’ve ever made at Tesla,” and that “the initial portion of the S-curve will be quite flat and long,” because most of the robot’s parts are new.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the bill of materials.** Industry analyses put a full-size humanoid at roughly $55,000 in parts, with actuators, the “muscles” that move each joint, making up about 56% of that cost.

clean_body: Peter, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. People ask me all the time why I left the Republican Party. They expect a simple answer. A single moment. A breaking point. There wasn't one. There were _hundreds._ I grew up believing the GOP stood for something. Fiscal discipline. Strong institutions. A belief that character counted, that the office was bigger than the man who held it. That's the party my parents raised me to respect.That party is gone. What's left is a party that no longer asks whether something is true, only whether it's loyal. A party where senators who once criticized Donald Trump in private now defend him in public because they're afraid of a primary. A party that has traded the Constitution for a cult of personality. I sat in rooms with these people. I watched the transformation happen in real time — principle by principle, surrender by surrender. This is not the party of my father, who believed in hard work and honest leaders. It is not even the party it was ten years ago. **It is Donald Trump's party now, full stop. And it is up to us to stop it from doing any more damage to this country.** That's why Resist Reclaim Rebuild is fighting in the districts where this fight will actually be decided — the battlegrounds where a MAGA rubber stamp can be replaced by someone who still believes in checks and balances. **[Will you chip in $10, $25 or whatever you can today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild take back these seats?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140652341/651173821/-323302678?refcode=260929_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjc2NTVkYzEtNDdjMC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=IE_-nbRtcYX7LyhbXDBO2zX1sALMZOeRTqlH6mcHa7s=)**

This is the governing body overseeing the National Science Foundation, one of the most important scientific institutions in the United States — **and he fired all of them. At once.** The National Science Board exists for a reason. It oversees billions in federal research funding, advises Congress on science policy, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars support real, evidence-based innovation. **Now that independence is being stripped away.** Let me say this clearly: When political leaders start dismantling independent science institutions, it doesn’t just hurt scientists. It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more. **As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics.** But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government. **This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF.** **[But I can’t take on that fight alone. We’re heading into a critical stretch of this campaign, and we need the resources to compete against entrenched interests that are perfectly comfortable ignoring science. clean_body: This is exactly why I’m running for Congress| | | = | | | There’s no sugarcoating it: Donald Trump fired all 22 members of the National Science Board. = = This is the governing body overseeing the National Science Foundation, one of the most important scientific institutions in the United States — and he fired all of them. At once. The National Science Board exists for a reason. It oversees billions in federal research funding, advises Congress on science policy, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars support real, evidence-based innovation. Now that independence is being stripped away. Let me say this clearly: When political leaders start dismantling independent science institutions, it doesn’t just hurt scientists. It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more. As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics. But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government. This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF. = = When we let science lead, people thrive. Let’s put facts back in charge — and build a Congress that reflects reason, reality, and hope. Washington Now Owns Pieces of 39 Companies. History Says Watch Who Gets the Money First.
A $27.7 billion government portfolio, an executive order on minerals, a 25-member alliance on AI supply chains, and a G20 at a Miami resort in December. The doors where new money enters the economy are moving. Here’s where.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |

|
---
There’s an old rule about money that the people who run it would rather you didn’t think about: **new money never reaches everyone at the same time.** It enters through a few doors first. The people standing at those doors spend it before prices rise. Everyone else gets it last, after prices have risen. Right now, Washington is building new doors. Here’s where they are.
The evidence board
| | Washington Is Becoming a Shareholder
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the portfolio.** As of September 30, the U.S. government holds about $27.7 billion in equity stakes across 39 companies, per a Council on Foreign Relations analysis. They include Intel ($8.9 billion, about 10%), MP Materials ($400 million), a USA Rare Earth deal worth up to $1.6 billion, Lithium Americas, Trilogy Metals, Vulcan Elements and a $1 billion stake in L3Harris’s missile unit.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the order.** Executive Order 14241, signed in March 2025, set “immediate measures to increase American mineral production.” Early 2026 brought Project Vault, a federal stockpile covering any mineral the Interior Department lists as critical.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the alliance.** The Pax Silica Declaration, signed in Washington in December 2025 by seven countries, had grown to 24 signatories plus the EU by July 2026. Its focus is supply chains for semiconductors, AI, critical minerals and energy, the inputs that modern power runs on.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the stage.** The G20 summit is set for December 14–15, 2026, at Trump National Doral in Miami, with the president as chair.

| | 1974–

Once oil was priced in dollars and recycled into Treasuries, the banks and defense contractors handling those flows built empires.
| | Now
---

Minerals, energy, chips and AI infrastructure: the sectors where Washington is now writing checks, signing treaties and taking stakes.

**Our theory:** when a government stops merely regulating an industry and starts owning pieces of it, it picks winners. Those companies get capital first, contracts first and political protection first. Savers holding cash get none of that, only the higher prices that follow. That gap is the oldest wealth transfer in finance, and it’s being rebuilt in real time.

| | LAST
---

Get the new money last, after prices have adjusted.

Peter, it’s Jon Ossoff.
I’m reaching out today to ask you to donate $5 to my reelection campaign, decisively rebuke the corrupt and failed Trump movement, and win this U.S. Senate race here in Georgia.
(If that’s all you need to hear, here’s the best link: [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-oct26**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261004-3-f&utm_campaign=em261004-3-f&t=2&akid=2997%2E5691347%2EMNTGpi))
If you’ve had enough of the weekly Watergate scandals and corruption...
If you want to stop Donald Trump’s corrupt agenda in its tracks and restore checks and balances in Washington...
If you’re tired of the Trumps (and their MAGA friends) using the office of the presidency to enrich themselves in a way we have never, ever seen in American history...
This is something you can do today to make a difference.
I first ran for Senate in Georgia in 2020 because I saw the danger in electing someone so profoundly unfit for the presidency, and to confront the corruption that made his rise possible. We defeated him, and I won.
Now we have to do it all again. The country is counting on Georgia.
And just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
